terms.label: CC Generic Entity MODEL::CLASS IN REPOSITORY
terms.definition: Any ENTITY name belonging to the repository. E.g. DAY TYPE, PROPERTY OF DAY, TIME BAND, VEHICLE TYPE, etc, are relevant instances of CLASS IN REPOSITORY in the context of version management. Notes: Unique Identifier of Class of ENTITY. There will only be a Single instance, which must be the class name, e.g. Day Type, Property of Day, etc

terms.label: CC Generic Entity MODEL::ENTITY
terms.definition: Any data instance to be managed in an operational Version Management System. When several data sources coexist (multimodality and/or interoperability), an ENTITY has to be related to a given DATA SOURCE in which it is defined. Notes: Date & time of last change to ENTITY. Notes: Date and time of creation of ENTITY. Notes: Identifier of ENTITY. Unique within a namespace.

terms.label: CC Generic Entity MODEL::TYPE OF ENTITY
terms.definition: Classification of ENTITies, for instance according to the domain in which they are defined or used. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ENTITY.

terms.label: CC Generic Version MODEL::ENTITY IN VERSION
terms.definition: The ENTITY associated to a given VERSION. Notes: Identifier of ENTITY IN VERSION. Notes: Nature of modification. Enumerated value : new | update | delete.

terms.label: CC Generic Version MODEL::TYPE OF VERSION
terms.definition: A classification of VERSIONs. E.g shareability of ENTITies between several versions. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF VERSION.

terms.label: CC Generic Version MODEL::VERSION
terms.definition: A group of operational data instances which share the same VALIDITY CONDITIONs. A version belongs to a unique VERSION FRAME and is characterised by a unique TYPE OF VERSION. Notes: Description of VERSION. Notes: End date of validity of VERSION. Notes: Identifier of VERSION. Notes: Name of VERSION. Notes: Status of VERSION. Enumerated value.

terms.label: CC Generic Version Frame MODEL::CLASS IN FRAME
terms.definition: The different CLASSEes IN REPOSITORY which can be relevant for corresponding VERSION FRAMEs. Notes: Identifier of the class (name) of a CLASS IN REPOSITORY belonging to a VERSION FRAME.

terms.label: CC Generic Version Frame MODEL::TYPE OF FRAME
terms.definition: A classification of VERSION FRAMEs according to a common purpose. E.g. line descriptions for line versions, vehicle schedules, operating costs. A TYPE OF FRAME is ruled by a unique TYPE OF VALIDITY. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF FRAME. Notes: Whether all contained instances or just deltas must be present. Notes: How long frames of this contents are valid for by default. Notes: How long frames of this contents are valid for by default. Notes: How version numbers should be used.

terms.label: CC Generic Version Frame MODEL::TYPE OF VALIDITY
terms.definition: A classification of the validity of TYPEs OF FRAME. E.g. frames for schedules designed for DAY TYPEs, for specific OPERATING DAYs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF VALIDITY.

terms.label: CC Generic Version Frame MODEL::VERSION FRAME
terms.definition: A set of VERSIONS referring to a same DATA SOURCE and belonging to the same TYPE OF FRAME. A FRAME may be restricted by VALIDITY CONDITIONs. Notes: Description of VERSION FRAME. Notes: Identifier of VERSION FRAME. Notes: Name of VERSION FRAME.

terms.label: CC Generic Validity MODEL::VALIDITY CONDITION
terms.definition: Condition used in order to characterise a given VERSION of a VERSION FRAME. A VALIDITY CONDITION consists of a parameter (e.g. date, triggering event, etc.) and its type of application (e.g. for, from, until, etc.). Notes: Description of VALIDITY CONDITION. Notes: Identifier of VALIDITY CONDITION. Notes: Name of VALIDITY CONDITION.

terms.label: CC Generic Validity MODEL::VALIDITY RULE PARAMETER
terms.definition: A user defined VALIDITY CONDITION used by a rule for selecting versions. E.g. river level #gt; 1,5 m and bad weather. Notes: ENTITY attribute used as input for VALIDITY PARAMETER. Notes: A fixed Value from comparison with for VALIDITY PARAMETER using operator Notes: Operator (GT EQ GE etc) to use to compare attribute with value. Notes: Identifier of VALIDITY RULE PARAMETER. Notes: Use object status to determine whether ENTITY is valid (Mutually Exclusive with operator and method) Notes: Method to use to evaluate whether ENTITY is valid (Mutually Exclusive with operator).

terms.label: CC Generic Validity MODEL::VALIDITY TRIGGER
terms.definition: External event defining a VALIDITY CONDITION. E.g exceptional flow of a river, bad weather, road closure for works. Notes: Identifier of VALIDITY TRIGGER. Notes: Identifier of type of event or other data associated with VALIDITY TRIGGER.

terms.label: CC Generic Delta MODEL::DELTA
terms.definition: A record of the detailed changes of a given ENTITY IN VERSION from one VERSION to the next one. A DELTA contains pairs of attributes' old values - new values. Notes: Identifier of ENTITY Delta.

terms.label: CC Generic Delta MODEL::TRACE
terms.definition: A way to record the context of the changes occurred in a given ENTITY instance, as regards the authors, the causes of the changes, etc., possibly accompanied by a descriptive text. Notes: Timestamp of when Object was Changed. Notes: Who made change. Notes: Description of context for change..

terms.label: CC Responsibility Role MODEL::RESPONSIBILITY ROLE
terms.definition: A particular role an ORGANISATION or an ORGANISATION PART is playing as regards certain data, for example data origination, data augmentation, data aggregation, data distribution, planning, operation, control, ownership etc). Notes: Identified of RESPONSIBILITY ROLE.

terms.label: CC Responsibility Role MODEL::RESPONSIBILITY ROLE ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The assignment of one or more roles to an ORGANISATION or an ORGANISATION PART as regards the responsibility it will have as regards specific data (e.g. ownership, planning, etc.) and the management of this data (e.g. distribution, updates, etc.). Notes: Identifier of RESPONSIBILITY ROLE ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: CC Responsibility Role MODEL::RESPONSIBILITY SET
terms.definition: A list of possible responsibilities over one or more ENTITies IN VERSION., resulting from the process of the assignment of RESPONSIBILITY ROLEs (such as data origination, ownership, etc) on specific data (instances) to ORGANISATIONs or ORGANISATION PARTs. Notes: Identifier of RESPONSIBILITY SET.

terms.label: CC Responsibility Role MODEL::TYPE OF RESPONSIBILITY ROLE
terms.definition: A classification of RESPONSIBILITY ROLEs, e.g. data ownership. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF RESPONSIBILITY ROLE.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::LINK
terms.definition: An oriented spatial object of dimension 1 with view to the overall description of a network, describing a connection between two POINTs. Notes: Distance along LINK Notes: Identifier of LINK. Notes: Name of LINK

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::TYPE OF LINK
terms.definition: A classification of LINKs to express the different functional roles of a LINK. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF LINK. Notes: Name of TYPE OF LINK.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::POINT
terms.definition: A 0-dimensional node of the network used for the spatial description of the network. POINTs may be located by a LOCATION in a given LOCATING SYSTEM. Notes: Identifier of POINT. Notes: Name of POINT.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::TYPE OF POINT
terms.definition: A classification of POINTs according to their functional purpose. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF POINT.. Notes: Name of TYPE OF POINT.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::POINT ON LINK
terms.definition: A POINT on a LINK which is not needed for LINK definition, but may be used for other purposes, e.g. for purposes of automatic vehicle monitoring, passenger information or for driver information. Notes: Distance of POINT along LINK. Notes: Identifier of POINT On Link. Notes: Name of POINT ON LINK. Notes: Order of POINT along link relative to other POINTs ON LINK

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::GROUP OF POINTS
terms.definition: A grouping of POINTs of a certainTYPE OF POINT and dedicated to a FUNCTIONAL PURPOSE. Notes: Identifier of GROUP of POINTs.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link MODEL::GROUP OF LINKS
terms.definition: A grouping of LINKs. E.g. one GROUP OF LINKs may be managed by a same AUTHORITY. Notes: Identifier of GROUP OF LINKs.

terms.definition: An ordered sequence either of POINTs or of LINKs, defining a path through the network. Notes: Distance of ROUTE SEQUENCE. Units are as specified for Frame. Default is SI Metres Notes: Identifier of LINK SEQUENCE. Notes: Name of LINK SEQUENCE. Notes: Short Name of LINK SEQUENCE.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link Sequence MODEL::LINK IN LINK SEQUENCE
terms.definition: The order of a LINK in a LINK SEQUENCE to which it belongs. Notes: Identifier of LINK in LINK SEQUENCE. Notes: Order of LINK in LINK SEQUENCE.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link Sequence MODEL::POINT IN LINK SEQUENCE
terms.definition: A POINT in a LINK SEQUENCE indicating its order in that particular LINK SEQUENCE. Notes: Identifier of POINT in LINK SEQUENCE. Notes: Order of POINT in LINK SEQUENCE within sequence.

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link Sequence MODEL::GROUP OF LINK SEQUENCES

terms.label: CC Generic Point & Link Sequence MODEL::TYPE OF LINK SEQUENCE
terms.definition: A classification of LINK SEQUENCEs used to define the different functions a LINK SEQUENCE may be used for. E.g. ROUTE, road, border line etc. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF LINK SEQUENCE. Notes: Name of TYPE OF LINK SEQUENCE.

terms.label: CC Generic Zone and Feature MODEL::ZONE
terms.definition: A two-dimensional PLACE within the service area of a public transport operator (administrative zone, TARIFF ZONE, ACCESS ZONE, etc.). Notes: Description of Zone Notes: Identifier of ZONE. Notes: Name of ZONE.

terms.label: CC Generic Zone and Feature MODEL::TARIFF ZONE
terms.definition: A ZONE used to define a zonal fare structure in a zone-counting or zone-matrix system. Notes: Identifier of TARIFF ZONE.

terms.label: CC Generic Zone and Feature MODEL::COMPLEX FEATURE
terms.definition: An aggregate of SIMPLE FEATUREs and/or other COMPLEX FEATUREs. Notes: Identifier of COMPLEX FEATURE.

terms.label: CC Generic Zone and Feature MODEL::TYPE OF ZONE
terms.definition: A classification of ZONEs. E.g. TARIFF ZONE, ADMINISTRATIVE ZONE. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ZONE.

terms.label: CC Generic Zone and Feature MODEL::SIMPLE FEATURE
terms.definition: An abstract representation of elementary objects related to the spatial representation of the network. POINTs (0-dimensional objects), LINKs (1-dimensional objects) and ZONEs (2-dimensional objects) may be viewed as SIMPLE FEATUREs. Notes: Identifier of SIMPLE FEATURE.

terms.label: CC Generic Projection MODEL::POINT PROJECTION
terms.definition: An oriented correspondence from one POINT of a source layer, onto a entity in a target layer: e.g. POINT, LINK, LINK SEQUENCE, COMPLEX FEATURE, within a defined TYPE OF PROJECTION. Notes: Distance along projection Notes: Identifier of POINT PROJECTION.

terms.label: CC Generic Projection MODEL::LINK PROJECTION
terms.definition: An oriented correspondence from one LINK of a source layer, onto an entity in a target layer: e.g. LINK SEQUENCE, COMPLEX FEATURE, within a defined TYPE OF PROJECTION. Notes: Identifier of LINK PROJECTION.

terms.label: CC Generic Projection MODEL::COMPLEX FEATURE PROJECTION
terms.definition: An oriented correspondence: from one COMPLEX FEATURE in the source layer, onto an entity in a target layer: e.g. POINT, COMPLEX FEATURE, within a defined TYPE OF PROJECTION. Notes: Identifier of COMPLEX FEATURE PROJECTION.

terms.label: CC Generic Projection MODEL::ZONE PROJECTION
terms.definition: An oriented correspondence: from one ZONE in a source layer, onto a target entity : e.g. POINT, COMPLEX FEATURE, within a defined TYPE OF PROJECTION. Notes: Identifier of ZONE PROJECTION.

terms.label: CC Generic Projection MODEL::LINE SHAPE
terms.definition: The graphical shape of a LINK obtained from a formula or other means, using the LOCATION of its limiting POINTs and depending on the LOCATING SYSTEM used for the graphical representation. Notes: Formula for calculating line e.g. Bezier Notes: Identifier of LINE SHAPE. Notes: Name of LINE SHAPE

terms.label: CC Generic Projection MODEL::TYPE OF PROJECTION
terms.definition: A classification of the projections according to their functional purpose, the source and target layers. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PROJECTION. Notes: Name of TYPE OF PROJECTION (e.g. Point Projection, Link Projection, etc).

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::ACCESSIBILITY ASSESSMENT
terms.definition: The accessibility characteristics of an entity used by passengers such as a STOP PLACE, or a STOP PLACE COMPONENT. Described by ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATIONs, and/or a set of SUITABILITies Notes: Identifier of ACCESSIBILITY ASSESSMENT. Notes: Whether the overall assessment is that there is Access for Mobility Impaired users.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::SUITABILITY
terms.definition: A statement of whether a particular USER NEED can be met. It can be used to state whether a SITE can be accessed by a passenger with a particular USER NEED. Notes: Identifier of SUITABILITY. Notes: Whether the USER NEED is met.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATION
terms.definition: A categorisation of the accessibility characteristics of a SITE, e.g. a STOP PLACE or a STOP PLACE COMPONENT to indicate its usability by passengers with specific needs, for example, those needing wheelchair access, step-free access or wanting to avoid confined spaces such as lifts. A small number of well-defined categories are used that are chosen to allow the consistent capture of data and the efficient computation of routes for different classes of user. Notes: Whether there are Audible Signs. Notes: Whether there is Escalator Free Access.. Notes: Identifier of ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATION. Notes: Whether there is Lift Free Access.. Notes: Whether there is Step Free Access.. Notes: Whether there are Visual Signs. Notes: Whether there is Access for Wheelchair users.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::USER NEED
terms.definition: A user's need for a particular SUITABILITY. Notes: Whether USER NEED is to be include or excluded. Notes: Identified of USER NEED. Notes: A relative ranking of the need that can be specified in some applications.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::ENCUMBRANCE NEED
terms.definition: A specific USER NEED, i.e. a requirement of a passenger travelling with luggage, animal or any other object requiring special arrangements to access public transport. Notes: Identifier of ENCUMBRANCE NEED. Notes: Type of Encumbrance need

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::MEDICAL NEED
terms.definition: A specific USER NEED, i.e. a requirement of a passenger as regards medical constraint (e.g. allergy) to access public transport . Notes: Identifier of MEDICAL NEED. Notes: Type of Medical need

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::MOBILITY NEED
terms.definition: A specific USER NEED, i.e. a constraint of a passenger as regards his mobility, e.g. wheelchair, assisted wheelchair, etc. Notes: Identifier of MOBILITY NEED. Notes: Type of Mobility need

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::PASSENGER ACCESSIBILITY NEED
terms.definition: A passenger's requirement for accessibility, comprising one or more USER NEEDs. For example, that he is unable to navigate stairs, or lifts, or has visual or auditory impairments. PASSENGER ACCESSIBILITY NEEDS can be used to derive an accessibility constraint for the passenger, allowing the computation of paths for passengers with specifically constrained mobility. Example: Wheelchair, No Lifts, No Stairs. Notes: Whether user has carer Notes: Identifier of PASSENGER ACCESSIBILITY NEED.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::PSYCHOSENSORY NEED
terms.definition: A specific USER NEED, i.e. a constraint of a passenger as regards his psycho-sensory impairments, such as visual impairment, auditory impairment, averse to confined spaces, etc. Notes: Identifier of PSYCHOSENSORY NEED. Notes: Type of Psychosensory need

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::TYPE OF ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATION
terms.definition: A classification for ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATIONs, e.g. audio, visual, step free, etc. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ACCESSIBILITY LIMITATION.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::TYPE OF SUITABILITY
terms.definition: A classification for SUITABILITY, i.e. assessments as regards a possible SUITABILITY of access according to USER NEEDS. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF SUITABILITY.

terms.label: CC Generic Accessibility MODEL::TYPE OF USER NEED
terms.definition: A classification of USER NEEDS. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF USER NEED.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::ACCESS END
terms.definition: Origin or destination end of an ACCESS link. May indicate a POINT and/or PLACE.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::TRANSFER END
terms.definition: End point of a TRANSFER.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::PLACE
terms.definition: A geographic place of any type which may be specified as the origin or destination of a trip. A PLACE may be represented as a POINT (dimension 0) , a road section (dimension 1) or a ZONE (dimension 2). Notes: Identifier of PLACE.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::TRANSFER
terms.definition: A couple of POINTs located sufficiently near that it may represent for a passenger a possibility to reach one of these POINTs when starting at the other one in a timescale which is realistic when carrying out a trip, e.g. ACCESS. Notes: Whether TRANSFER can be traversed in both directions Notes: Default interval to make transfer. Notes: Description of TRANSFER. Notes: Distance of TRANSFER link Notes: Time for a traveller familiar with journey to make transfer. Notes: Identifier of TRANSFER. Notes: Time for a mobility impaired traveller to make transfer. Notes: Name of TRANSFER. Notes: Time for a traveller unfamiliar with journey to make transfer.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::ACCESS
terms.definition: The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to access or leave the public transport system. This link may be used during a trip for:- the walking movement of a passenger from a PLACE (origin of the trip) to a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (origin of the PT TRIP), or- the walking movement from a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (destination of the PT TRIP) to a PLACE (destination of the trip). Notes: Identifier of ACCESS link.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::TYPE OF PLACE
terms.definition: A classification for PLACEs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PLACE.

terms.label: CC Generic Place MODEL::TYPE OF TRANSFER
terms.definition: A classification for TRANSFER. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF TRANSFER.

terms.label: CC Transport Mode MODEL::ACCESS MODE
terms.definition: A characterisation of the passenger movement according to the means of transport different from public transport (e.g. walk, bicycle, etc) Notes: Identifier of ACCESS MODE.

terms.label: CC Transport Mode MODEL::MODE
terms.definition: Any means of transport. Notes: Identifier of TRANSPORT MODE. Notes: Name of MODE.

terms.label: CC Transport Mode MODEL::VEHICLE MODE
terms.definition: A characterisation of the public transport operation according to the means of transport (bus, tram, metro, train, ferry, ship). Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE MODE.

terms.definition: A non-advertised mode of operation of vehicles by persons using their own vehicle. Notes: Identifier of PERSONAL MODE OF OPERATION.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Mode MODEL::SCHEDULED OPERATION
terms.definition: The operation of a transportation using any kind of vehicle with a predefined time table. Notes: Identifier of SCHEDULED OPERATION.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Mode MODEL::TYPE OF MODE OF OPERATION
terms.definition: A classification for a MODE OF OPERATION. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF MODE OF OPERATION. .

terms.label: CC NM Transport Mode MODEL::VEHICLE POOLING
terms.definition: An ALTERNATIVE MODE OF OPERATION of a privately-owned vehicle consisting in sharing the vehicle for a trip between the driver who is at the same time performing a trip and at least another traveller. Note that Chauffeured Car and Taxi are special types of VEHICLE POOLING (with a dedicated TYPE OF OPERATION). Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE POOLING.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Mode MODEL::VEHICLE RENTAL
terms.definition: An ALTERNATIVE MODE OF OPERATION of a vehicle, part of a FLEET (in general privately owned), available for use for a certain period of time and fee, with the constraint to bring it back at specified agencies. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE RENTAL.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Mode MODEL::VEHICLE SHARING
terms.definition: Short term VEHICLE RENTAL where the vehicle can be taken from and parked at different places in the urban area, possibly without the constraint to bring back the vehicle to a specific location. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE SHARING.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::CONTROL CENTRE
terms.definition: An ORGANISATION PART for an operational team who are responsible for issuing commands to control the services. Notes: Identifier of CONTROL CENTRE.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::TRANSPORT ORGANISATION
terms.definition: Specialisation of ORGANISATION providing transport services related to particular modes of operation. Notes: Identifier of ORGANISATION.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::AUTHORITY
terms.definition: The organisation under which the responsibility of organising the transport service in a certain area is placed. Notes: Identifier of AUTHORITY.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::GROUP OF OPERATORS
terms.definition: A group of OPERATORs having for instance common schemes for fare collection or passenger information. Notes: Category of GROUP OF OPERATORs. Notes: Identifier of GROUP OF OPERATORs.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::OPERATOR
terms.definition: A company providing public transport services. Notes: Identifier of OPERATOR.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::OPERATING DEPARTMENT
terms.definition: A specific DEPARTMENT which administers certain LINEs. Notes: Identifier of OPERATING DEPARTMENT.

terms.label: CC NM Transport Organisations MODEL::OPERATIONAL CONTEXT
terms.definition: Characterization of a set of operational objects, such as timing or links determined either by a DEPARTMENT or by an ORGANISATIONAL UNIT. Notes: Identifier of OPERATIONAL CONTEXT. Notes: Name of OPERATIONAL CONTEXT. Notes: Short name of OPERATIONAL CONTEXT.

terms.label: TM CC NM Additional Organisation MODEL
terms.definition: ORGANISATION being neither an AUTHORITY, neither a public transport OPERATOR.

terms.label: CC NM Additional Organisations MODEL::OTHER ORGANISATION
terms.definition: Generic ORGANISATION being neither an AUTHORITY, neither a public transport OPERATOR (TRAVEL AGENT, MANAGEMENT AGENT, etc.). Notes: Identifier of OTHER ORGANISATION.

terms.label: CC NM Additional Organisations MODEL::MANAGEMENT AGENT
terms.definition: Specialisation of ORGANISATION for MANAGEMENT AGENTs. Notes: Identifier of MANAGEMENT AGENT.

terms.label: CC NM Additional Organisations MODEL::SERVICED ORGANISATION
terms.definition: A public or private organisation for which public transport services are provided on specific days, e.g. a school, univesirty or works. Notes: Identifier of TRAVEL AGENT.

terms.label: CC NM Additional Organisations MODEL::TRAVEL AGENT
terms.definition: Specialisation of ORGANISATION for TRAVEL AGENT Notes: Identifier of SERVICED ORGANISATION.

terms.label: CC NM Additional Organisations MODEL::ORGANISATION DAY TYPE
terms.definition: DAY TYPE that is defined in terms of operation or not operation of a referenced SERVICED ORGANISATION. Notes: Identifier of DAY TYPE. Notes: Transport Service required for ORGANISATION on this DAY TYPE .

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::FACILITY REQUIREMENT
terms.definition: A classification of public transport vehicles according to the facilities available on the vehicle. Notes: Identifier of a SERVICE FACILITY REQUIREMENT.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::MANOEUVRING REQUIREMENT
terms.definition: A classification of requirements for a public transport VEHICLE according to the Maneuvering capabilities of the vehicle. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE MANOEUVRING REQUIREMENT. Notes: Minimum length needed to accommodate VEHICLE. Notes: Minimum width needed by VEHICLE TYPE to overtake. Notes: Minimum turning circle needed to turn a VEHICLE, Notes: Whether VEHICLE must be Reversible.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::PASSENGER CARRYING REQUIREMENT
terms.definition: A classification of requirements for a public transport vehicle according to the passenger carrying capabilities of the vehicle. Notes: Whether VEHICLE needs to have lift or ramp for wheelchair access. Notes: Identifier of PASSENGER CARRYING REQUIREMENT. Notes: Whether VEHICLE needs to be low floor. Notes: Minimum number of seated passengers that needs to be provided.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::TYPE OF FUEL
terms.definition: A classification for a fleet of VEHICLEs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF FUEL.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::VEHICLE
terms.definition: A public transport vehicle used for carrying passengers. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE. Notes: Name of VEHICLE. Notes: Short Name of VEHICLE. Notes: Registration number of VEHICLE.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::SIMPLE VEHICLE TYPE
terms.definition: A classification of a personal transport means (cycle, scooter, skis, etc) according to its properties. Notes: Identifier of SIMPLE VEHICLE TYPE.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::TRANSPORT TYPE
terms.definition: A classification of transport vehicles according to their properties. Notes: Description of TRANSPORT TYPE. Notes: Identifier of TRANSPORT TYPE. Notes: Length of TRANSPORT TYPE. Notes: Name of TRANSPORT TYPE. Notes: Range between fuel refills. Notes: Maximum number of seated passengers that can be carried by a Vehicle of this type Notes: Whether TRANSPORT TYPE is self-propelled. Notes: Short Name of TRANSPORT TYPE. Notes: Maximum number of standing passengers that can be carried by a VEHICLE of this type

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::VEHICLE TYPE
terms.definition: A classification of public transport vehicles according to the vehicle scheduling requirements in mode and capacity (e.g. standard bus, double-deck, ...). Notes: Whether VEHICLE TYPE has lift or ramp for wheelchair access. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE TYPE. Notes: Whether VEHICLE TYPE is low floor Notes: Whether VEHICLE TYPE has a reversing direction. Notes: Maximum number of passengers needing special places that can be carried by a Vehicle of this type Notes: Maximum number of passengers needing special places that can be carried by a Vehicle of this type

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::VEHICLE MODEL
terms.definition: A classification of public transport vehicles of the same VEHICLE TYPE, e.g. according to equipment specifications or model generation. Notes: Description of VEHICLE MODEL. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE MODEL. Notes: Manufacturer of VEHICLE MODEL. Notes: Name of VEHICLE MODEL.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::VEHICLE EQUIPMENT PROFILE
terms.definition: Each instantiation of this entity gives the number of items of one TYPE OF EQUIPMENT a VEHICLE MODEL should contain for a given PURPOSE OF EQUIPMENT PROFILE. The set of instantiations for one VEHICLE MODEL and one purpose gives one complete 'profile'. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE EQUIPMENT PROFILE. Notes: Text for VEHICLE EQUIPMENT PROFILE. Notes: Units (number of instances of equipment), for VEHICLE EQUIPMENT PROFILE.

terms.label: CC NM Vehicle Type MODEL::PURPOSE OF EQUIPMENT PROFILE
terms.definition: A functional purpose which requires a certain set of equipment of different types put together in a VEHICLE EQUIPMENT PROFILE. Notes: Identifier of PURPOSE OF EQUIPMENT PROFILE.

terms.definition: A specification of the order of TRAIN ELEMENTs in a TRAIN. Notes: Description of TRAIN COMPONENT. Notes: Identifier of TRAIN COMPONENT. Notes: Label of TRAIN COMPONENT. Notes: Name of TRAIN COMPONENT. Notes: Order of TRAIN COMPONENT in TRAIN.

terms.label: CC NM Train MODEL::TYPE OF TRAIN ELEMENT
terms.definition: A classification of TRAIN ELEMENTs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE of TRAIN.

terms.label: CC NM Train MODEL::COMPOUND TRAIN
terms.definition: A VEHICLE TYPE composed of a sequence of more than one vehicles of the type TRAIN. Notes: Identifier of COMPOUND TRAIN.

terms.label: CC NM Train MODEL::TRAIN IN COMPOUND TRAIN
terms.definition: The specification of the order of TRAINs in a COMPOUND TRAIN. Notes: Description of TRAIN COMPONENT. Notes: Identifier of TRAIN in COMPOUND TRAIN. Notes: Label of TRAIN COMPONENT. terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::SITE ELEMENT
terms.definition: A type of ADRESSABLE PLACE specifying common properties of a SITE or a SITE COMPONENT to describe it, including accessibility. Notes: Whether all areas of component are accessible in a Wheelchair. Notes: Whether element is covered or outdoors. Notes: Name of nearest Cross road or crossing street on which SITE is on which can be used to locate stop. Notes: Whether element is within a gated area. Notes: Identifier of SITE ELEMENT. Notes: Image associated with SITE ELEMENT. Notes: Name of nearby Landmark. Notes: How element is lit. Notes: Suffix to use on Name. Notes: Number of people that can be in component at a time. Notes: Whether SITE ELEMENT can be used by the general public. Notes: URL associated with SITE ELEMENT.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::SITE
terms.definition: A well known PLACE to which passengers may refer to indicate the origin or a destination of a trip. Notes: Whether the site is central to the locality, referenced at town centre. Notes: Identifier of SITE. Notes: Locale setting time zone, default language etc, for the STOP PLACE. Notes: Type of SITE.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::SERVICE SITE
terms.definition: A sub-type of SITE which is of specific interest for the operator (e.g. where a joint service or a joint fee is proposed)., other than a STOP PLACE. Notes: Identifier of SERVICE SITE.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::SITE COMPONENT
terms.definition: An element of a SITE describing a part of its structure. SITE COMPONENTs share common properties for data management, accessibility and other features. Notes: Identifier of SITE COMPONENT.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::ENTRANCE
terms.definition: A physical entrance or exit to/from a SITE. May be a door, barrier, gate or other recognizable point of access. Notes: Whether ENTRANCE is near Drop off point. Notes: Whether there is a dropped curb outside ENTRANCE. Notes: Type of ENTRANCE. Notes: Height of ENTRANCE. Notes: Identifier of ENTRANCE. Notes: Whether ENTRANCE can be used for entry to SITE. Notes: Whether ENTRANCE can be used for exit from SITE. Notes: Whether ENTRANCE opens externally. Notes: Label of ENTRANCE. Notes: Width of ENTRANCE.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::VEHICLE ENTRANCE
terms.definition: A physical entrance or exit to/from a STOP PLACE for a VEHICLE. May be a door, barrier, gate or other recognizable point of access. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE ENTRANCE. Notes: Whether VEHICLE ENTRANCE can be used by Private VEHICLEs.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::LEVEL
terms.definition: An identified storey (ground, first, basement, mezzanine, etc) within an interchange building or SITE on which SITE COMPONENTs reside. A PATH LINK may connect components on different levels. Notes: Whether all areas of component are accessible in a Wheelchair. Notes: Further descriptive note about LEVEL Notes: Identifier of LEVEL. Notes: Name of LEVEL. Notes: Name of a nearby landmark which can be used to refer to SITE Notes: Short Name of LEVEL.

terms.label: NT NM Site MODEL (Extensions)::ACCESS ZONE
terms.definition: A ZONE for which the duration to cover any ACCESS link to a particular SCHEDULED STOP POINT is the same. Notes: Identifier of ACCESS ZONE.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING
terms.definition: Designated locations for leaving vehicles such as cars, motorcycles and bicycles. Notes: Url for booking. Notes: List of cards accepted Notes: Currencies accepted. Notes: Default Currency for payment Notes: Whether car park has recharging points Notes: Whether there is free parking out of hours Notes: Identifier of PARKING. Notes: Number of Parking levels, Notes: Whether overnight PARKING is allowed. Notes: Layout type of PARKING. Notes: How to pay for PARKING. Notes: How to reserve for PARKING. Notes: Nature of PARKING. Notes: Phone Payment details Notes: Principal Capacity of PARKING. Notes: Whether PARKING is prohibited for any Hazard. Notes: Whether there is real-time occupancy data for PARKING. Notes: Whether the parking is secure Notes: Total Capacity of PARKING.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING COMPONENT
terms.definition: Generic COMPONENT of a PARKING (e.g. PARKING AREA or PARKING BAY) Notes: Identifier of PARKING COMPONENT. Notes: Maximum height of Vehicle to use Parking Component. Notes: Maximum length of Vehicle to use Parking Component. Notes: Maximum weight of Vehicle to use Parking Component. Notes: Maximum height of Vehicle to use Parking Component. Notes: Identifier of PARKING COMPONENT for payment purposes, eg for SMS

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING COMPONENT PROPERTIES
terms.definition: A set of public facing characteristics of a PARKING COMPONENT facilitating the traveller the recognition of the component. Notes: Identifier of PARKING COMPONENT PROPERTIES . Notes: Whether the PARKING COMPONENT is marked. Notes: Characterisation of the priortiy to park according to some policy rules. Notes: Number or name of the PARKING COMPONENT.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING AREA
terms.definition: A marked zone within a PARKING containing PARKING BAYs. Notes: Identifier of PARKING AREA. Notes: Total Capacity of PARKING AREA.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING BAY
terms.definition: A place to park an individual vehicle. Notes: Height of BAY. Notes: Identifier of PARKING BAY. Notes: Length of BAY. Notes: Width of BAY.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING CAPACITY
terms.definition: PARKING properties providing information about its CAPACITY. Notes: Identifier of PARKING CAPACITY Notes: Number of parking spaces specified by this PARKING CAPACITY Notes: Types of Users of PARKING PROPERTies.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING PASSENGER ENTRANCE
terms.definition: An entrance to the PARKING for passengers on foot or other out-of-vehicle mode, such as wheelchair. Notes: Identifier of PARKING PASSENGER ENTRANCE.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING PROPERTIES
terms.definition: PARKING specific properties other than its capacity. Notes: Identifier of PARKING PROPERTies. Notes: Maximum Stay specified by this PARKING PROPERTies. Notes: Types of Users of PARKING PROPERTies.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::PARKING ENTRANCE FOR VEHICLES
terms.definition: An entrance for vehicles to the PARKING from the road. Notes: Identifier of PARKING VEHICLE ENTRANCE.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::TYPE OF PARKING
terms.definition: A classification for a PARKING. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PARKING.

terms.label: NT NM Parking MODEL (Extensions)::TYPE OF PARKING STAY
terms.definition: A classification for a stay in parking, e.g.short term, long term, etc.. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PARKING STAY.

terms.label: NM Meeting Place MODEL::VEHICLE SHARING PARKING BAY

terms.label: NT Network Restriction MODEL::MEETING RESTRICTION
terms.definition: A pair of INFRASTRUCTURE LINKs where vehicles of specified VEHICLE TYPEs are not allowed to meet. Notes: Identifier of MEETING RESTRICTION.

terms.label: NT Network Restriction MODEL::OVERTAKING POSSIBILITY
terms.definition: NETWORK RESTRICTION specifying a POINT or a LINK where vehicles of specified VEHICLE TYPEs are or are not allowed to overtake each other. Notes: Identifier of OVERTAKING RESTRICTION. Notes: Width at overtaking point

terms.label: NT Network Restriction MODEL::IMPOSSIBLE MANOEUVRE
terms.definition: A specification of impossible move for a certain type of vehicle. It specifies from which INFRASTRUCTURE LINK to which other (adjacent) INFRASTRUCTURE LINK a certain VEHICLE TYPE cannot proceed, due to physical restrictions. Notes: Identifier of IMPOSSIBLE MANOEUVRE.

terms.label: NT Network Restriction MODEL::VEHICLE TYPE AT POINT
terms.definition: The number of vehicles of a specified VEHICLE TYPE which may wait at a specified POINT at any one time. If the capacity is 0, then that type of vehicle may not stop there. Notes: Number of vehicles allowed at a given time at VEHICLE TYPE AT POINT. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE TYPE AT POINT restriction.

terms.label: NT Line Network MODEL::LINE NETWORK
terms.definition: The topological structure of a NETWORK as a graph of LINE SECTIONs. This allows the branches and loops of a LINE to be described as a whole. Notes: Description of LINE NETWORK. . Notes: Identifier of LINE NETWORK. Notes: Name of LINE NETWORK.

terms.label: NT Line Network MODEL::LINE SECTION
terms.definition: A part of a NETWORK comprising an edge between two nodes. Not directional. Notes: Identifier of LINE SECTION. Notes: Type of LINE SECTION.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::TURN STATION
terms.definition: A place (often a terminus)where a vehicle can reverse its direction (from a ROUTE to another of opposite DIRECTION). Notes: Identifier of TURN STATION. Notes: Distance available to turnaround in TURN STATION.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::DIRECTION
terms.definition: A classification for the general orientation of ROUTEs. Notes: Identifier of DIRECTION. Notes: Name of DIRECTION.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::ROUTE POINT
terms.definition: A POINT used to define the shape of a ROUTE through the network. Notes: Whether points is a border crossing Notes: Identifier of ROUTE POINT. Notes: Whether ROUTE POINT is flagged as a via point

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::ROUTE LINK
terms.definition: An oriented link between two ROUTE POINTs allowing the definition of a unique path through the network. Notes: Distance of ROUTE LINK. Units are as specified for Frame. Default is SI Metres Notes: Identifier of ROUTE LINK.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::ROUTE
terms.definition: An ordered list of located POINTs defining one single path through the road (or rail) network. A ROUTE may pass through the same POINT more than once. Notes: Description of ROUTE. Notes: Identifier of ROUTE.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::POINT ON ROUTE
terms.definition: A ROUTE POINT used to define a ROUTE with its order on that ROUTE. Notes: Identifier of POINT ON ROUTE. Notes: Order of POINT ON ROUTE in a given ROUTE.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::GROUP OF LINES
terms.definition: A grouping of lines which will be commonly referenced for a specific purpose. Notes: Identifier of a GROUP of LINEs.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::NETWORK
terms.definition: A named grouping of LINEs under which a transport network is known. Notes: Identifier of NETWORK. Notes: Name of NETWORK.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::LINE
terms.definition: A group of ROUTEs which is generally known to the public by a similar name or number. Notes: Description of LINE. Notes: Identifier of LINE. Notes: A URL associated with the LINE. Notes: Whether real-time data is available for LINE. Notes: Name of LINE. Notes: Short Name of LINE.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::DESTINATION DISPLAY
terms.definition: An advertised destination of a specific JOURNEY PATTERN, usually displayed on a headsign or at other on-board locations. Notes: Text to display to DRIVER. Notes: Front of vehicle text associated of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Identifier of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Name of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Additional short CODE associated with DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Short Name of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Text to display on side of vehicle associated with DESTINATION DISPLAY.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::DESTINATION DISPLAY VARIANT
terms.definition: An advertised destination of a specific JOURNEY PATTERN, usually displayed on a headsign or at other on-board locations. Notes: Way a NOTICE is delivered, characterized by the delivery medium (voice, printed material, etc). Notes: Front of vehicle text associated of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Identifier of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Name of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Short Name of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Text to display on side of vehicle associated with DESTINATION DISPLAY.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::ALLOWED LINE DIRECTION
terms.definition: An allowed DIRECTION that can be used on a given ROUTE. This can be used to validate the selection of allowed values. Notes: Identifier of ALLOWED LINE DIRECTION.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::TYPE OF LINE
terms.definition: A classification for LINEs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF LINE.

terms.label: NT Route MODEL::VIA
terms.definition: A secondary heading relevant for a certain part of the JOURNEY PATTERN advertising an onward intermediate destination to supplement the advertised (final) destination of DESTINATION DISPLAY. Notes: Identifier of VIA. Notes: Name of VIA. Notes: Type of Via

terms.label: ND Network Description MODEL
terms.definition: The Network Description Model describes the basic physical network and is divided into a number of separate submodels covering different aspects of the Network. For ease of understanding, the submodels are presented one at a time, each describing only a small set of related concepts.

terms.label: NT Flexible Network MODEL::FLEXIBLE ROUTE
terms.definition: Specialisation of ROUTE for flexible service. May include both point and zonal areas and ordered and unordered sections. Notes: Type of FLEXIBLE ROUTE. Notes: Identifier of FLEXIBLE ROUTE.

terms.label: NT Flexible Network MODEL::FLEXIBLE LINE
terms.definition: Specialisation of LINE for flexible service. As all the service on a LINE may not all be flexible, flexibility itself is described at JOURNEY PATTERN level (meaning that a separate JOURNEY PATTERN is needed for each type of flexibility available for the line). Types of flexible services are : - Virtual line service - Flexible service with main route - Corridor service - Fixed stop area-wide flexible service - Free area-wide flexible service - Mixed types of flexible service - Mixed type of flexible and regular services Notes: Type of FLEXIBLE LINE. Notes: Identifier of FLEXIBLE LINE.

terms.label: NT Flexible Network MODEL::FLEXIBLE POINT PROPERTIES
terms.definition: Set of characteristics describing the possible flexibility of POINTs. A composition is used with POINT in order to avoid multiple inheritance. Notes: Identifier of a FLEXIBLE POINT PROPERTIES. Notes: Whether the POINT may be skipped. Notes: Whether the POINT is on the main ROUTE. Notes: Whether the POINT represents a FLEXIBLE ZONE. Notes: Whether the ZONE is defined by a GROUP of POINT (true) or a geographical zone defined by its boundary.

terms.label: NT Flexible Network MODEL::FLEXIBLE LINK PROPERTIES
terms.definition: Set of properties describing the flexible characteristics of a LINK. A composition is used with LINK in order to avoid multiple inheritance and a type explosion of link subtypes Notes: Type of FLEXIBLE ROUTE LINK. Notes: Identifier of a FLEXIBLE LINK PROPERTIES. Notes: Whether the LINK may be skipped. Notes: Whether the LINK is on the main ROUTE of the LINE. Notes: Whether the connection with the road infrastructure is not defined.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::ACTIVATION POINT
terms.definition: A POINT where a control process is activated when a vehicle passes it. Equipment may be needed for the activation. Notes: Number of ACTIVATION POINT. Notes: Identifier of ACTIVATION POINT. Notes: Short Name of ACTIVATION POINT.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::ACTIVATION LINK
terms.definition: A LINK where a control process is activated when a vehicle passes it. Notes: Identifier of ACTIVATION LINK.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::BEACON POINT
terms.definition: A POINT where a beacon or similar device to support the automatic detection of vehicles passing by is located. Notes: Identifier of BEACON POINT.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT
terms.definition: A POINT where the traffic flow can be influenced. Examples are: traffic lights (lanterns), barriers. Notes: Identifier of TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::ACTIVATION ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: An assignment of an ACTIVATION POINT/LINK to an ACTIVATED EQUIPMENT related on its turn to a TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT. The considered ACTIVATION POINT/LINK will be used to influence the control process for that TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT (e.g. to fix priorities as regards the processing of competing requests from different ACTIVATION POINTs/LINKs). Notes: Identifier of ACTIVATION ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Order of ASSIGNMENT relative to other ASSIGNMENTs.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::ACTIVATED EQUIPMENT
terms.definition: An equipment activated by the passage of a vehicle at an ACTIVATION POINT or on an ACTIVATION LINK. Notes: Identifier of ACTIVATED EQUIPMENT.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::TYPE OF ACTIVATION
terms.definition: A classification of real-time processes that are activated when vehicles passes an ACTIVATION POINT or an ACTIVATION LINK. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ACTIVATION.

terms.label: NT Activation MODEL::TYPE OF TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT
terms.definition: A classification of TRAFFIC CONTROL POINTs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF TRAFFIC CONTROL POINT.

terms.label: NT Vehicle & Crew Point MODEL::CREW BASE
terms.definition: A place where operating employees (e.g. drivers) report on and register their work. Notes: Identifier of CREW BASE. Notes: Name of CREW BASE.

terms.label: NT Vehicle & Crew Point MODEL::GARAGE
terms.definition: A facility used for parking and maintaining vehicles. PARKING POINTs in a GARAGE are called GARAGE POINTs. Notes: Identifier of GARAGE. Notes: Name of GARAGE.

terms.label: NT Vehicle & Crew Point MODEL::RELIEF POINT
terms.definition: A TIMING POINT where a relief is possible, i.e. a driver may take on or hand over a vehicle. The vehicle may sometimes be left unattended. Notes: Identifier of RELIEF POINT.

terms.label: NT Vehicle & Crew Point MODEL::PARKING POINT
terms.definition: A TIMING POINT where vehicles may stay unattended for a long time. A vehicle's return to park at a PARKING POINT marks the end of a BLOCK. Notes: Identifier of PARKING POINT.

terms.label: NT Vehicle & Crew Point MODEL::GARAGE POINT
terms.definition: A subtype of PARKING POINT located in a GARAGE. Notes: Identifier of GARAGE POINT.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::STOP PLACE SPACE
terms.definition: A physical area within a STOP PLACE, for example, a QUAY, BOARDING POSITION, ACCESS SPACE or EQUIPMENT PLACE. Notes: Whether Passengers may use the component when Alighting from vehicle transport. Notes: Whether Passengers may use the component for Boarding vehicle transport. Notes: Alternative Local Label given to Component, e.g. a Point Letter on a stop.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::STOP PLACE
terms.definition: A place comprising one or more locations where vehicles may stop and where passengers may board or leave vehicles or prepare their trip. A STOP PLACE will usually have one or more wellknown names. Notes: Whether STOP PLACE is a border crossing. Notes: Identifier of a STOP PLACE. Notes: Categorisation of the stop as having topographic limitations which may affect its use in journey planners Notes: Default relative weighting to be used for STOP PLACE.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::STOP PLACE COMPONENT
terms.definition: An element of a STOP PLACE describing part of its structure. STOP PLACE COMPONENTs share common properties for data management, accessibility and other features. Notes: Label given to SITE COMPONENT. Notes: Other MODEs associated with STOP PLACE COMPONENT.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::STOP PLACE ENTRANCE
terms.definition: A physical entrance or exit to/from a STOP PLACE for a Passenger. May be a door, barrier, gate or other recognizable point of access. Notes: Identifier of STOP PLACE ENTRANCE.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::STOP PLACE VEHICLE ENTRANCE
terms.definition: A physical entrance or exit to/from a STOP PLACE for a vehicle. Notes: Identifier of STOP PLACE VEHICLE ENTRANCE.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::ACCESS SPACE
terms.definition: A passenger area within a STOP PLACE such as a concourse or booking hall, immigration hall or security area that is accessible by passengers, but without a direct access to vehicles. Direct access to a VEHICLE is always from a QUAY and/or BOARDING POSITION. An ACCESS SPACE may be a Room, Hall, Concourse, Corridor, or bounded open space within a STOP PLACE. Notes: Type of ACCESS SPACE. Notes: Identifier of ACCESS SPACE.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::QUAY
terms.definition: A place such as platform, stance, or quayside where passengers have access to PT vehicles, Taxi, cars or other means of transportation. A QUAY may serve one or more VEHICLE STOPPING PLACEs and be associated with one or more SCHEDULED STOP POINTS. A QUAY may contain other sub QUAYs. A child QUAY must be physically contained within its parent QUAY. Notes: Bearing of street relative to QUAY in degrees. Notes: Bearing of street relative to QUAY in compass quadrant. Notes: Destination shown on QUAY. Notes: Identifier of QUAY.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::BOARDING POSITION
terms.definition: A location within a QUAY from which passengers may directly board, or onto which passengers may directly alight from a VEHICLE. Notes: Identifier of BOARDING POSITION.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::TYPE OF PASSAGE
terms.definition: A classification for spaces to express how the space can be used as a passage (e.g. pathway, corridor, overpass, underpass, tunnel, etc.). Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PASSAGE.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::TYPE OF STOP PLACE
terms.definition: A classification for STOP PLACEs (e.g. complex, simple, multimodal, etc). Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF STOP PLACE.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::TYPE OF BOARDING POSITION
terms.definition: A classification for BOARDING POSITIONs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF BOARDING POSITION.

terms.label: NT Stop Place MODEL::TYPE OF QUAY
terms.definition: A classification for QUAYs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF QUAY.

terms.label: NT Flexible Stop Place MODEL::FLEXIBLE STOP PLACE
terms.definition: A specialisation of the STOP PLACE describing a stop of a FLEXIBLE SERVICE. It may be composed of FLEXIBLE AREAs or HAIL AND RIDE AREAs identifying the catchment areas for flexible services (when they use areas or flexible quays). Some FLEXIBLE SERVICE also use regular STOP PLACEs for their stops. When assigned to a SCHEDULED STOP POINT the corresponding SCHEDULED STOP POINT is supposed to be a ZONE (the centroid point of the ZONE being the SCHEDULED STOP POINT). Notes: Identifier of a FLEXIBLE STOP PLACE. Notes: Locale setting time zone, default language etc, for the FLEXIBLE STOP PLACE. Notes: Suffix to use on Name.

terms.label: NT Flexible Stop Place MODEL::FLEXIBLE QUAY
terms.definition: A physical ZONE such as a section of a road where a flexible service is available on demand. The existence of the zone makes the services visible to journey planners looking for available services for an area. Notes: Whether Passengers may use the FLEXIBLE QUAY for Alighting from vehicle transport. Notes: Whether Passengers may use the FLEXIBLE QUAY for Boarding vehicle transport. Notes: Identifier of a FLEXIBLE QUAY. Notes: Suffix to use on Name.

terms.label: NT Flexible Stop Place MODEL::FLEXIBLE AREA
terms.definition: Specialisation of a FLEXIBLE QUAY (which is abstract) to identify what is the catchment area for a flexible service (so that a stop finder can find the nearest available types of transport). It is a named zone visited by a particular mode of transport. It is part of the SITE data set rather than the service data set, since it can be defined and exists independently of an actual service. Notes: Identifier of a Flexible AREA.

terms.label: NT Flexible Stop Place MODEL::FLEXIBLE STOP ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The allocation of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (i.e. a STOP POINT of a SERVICE PATTERN or JOURNEY PATTERN) to a specific FLEXIBLE STOP PLACE, and also possibly a FLEXIBLE AREA or HAIL AND RIDE AREA. May be subject to a VALIDITY CONDITION. Notes: Identifier of FLEXIBLE STOP ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: NT Flexible Stop Place MODEL::HAIL AND RIDE AREA
terms.definition: Specialisation of a FLEXIBLE QUAY to identify what is the catchment zone for a hail and ride service (so that a stop finder can find the nearest available types of transport). It is a named zone visited by a particular mode of transport and may be designated by a start point and end point on the road It is part of the Site data set rather than the service data set, since it can be defined and exists indepently of an actual service. Notes: Compass Bearing associated with a HAIL AND RIDE AREA. Notes: Compass Octant associated with a HAIL AND RIDE AREA. Notes: Identifier of a HAIL AND RIDE AREA.

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST
terms.definition: A type of PLACE to or through which passengers may wish to navigate as part of their journey and which is modelled in detail by journey planners. Notes: Identifier of :POINT OF INTEREST.

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST SPACE
terms.definition: Specialisation of POINT OF INTEREST COMPONENT for SPACEs. A physical area within the POINT OF INTEREST, such as a concourse. Notes: Identifier of POINT OF INTEREST ACCESS SPACE.

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST ENTRANCE
terms.definition: Specialisation of ENTRANCE to enter/exit a POINT OF INTEREST. Notes: Identifier of a POINT OF INTEREST ENTRANCE

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST VEHICLE ENTRANCE
terms.definition: A physical entrance or exit to/from a POINT OF INTEREST for vehicles . Notes: Identifier of a POINT OF INTEREST VEHICLE ENTRANCE.

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION
terms.definition: A classification of a POINT OF INTEREST that may be used in a CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY to categorise the point by nature of interest using a systematic taxonomy, for example Museum, Football, Stadium. Notes: Identifier of a POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION. Notes: Short Name of a POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION.

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY
terms.definition: A logical hierarchy for organizing POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATIONs. A POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION can belong to more than one hierarchy. Notes: Identifier of a POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION HIERARCHY.

terms.label: NT Point Of Interest MODEL::POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBERSHIP
terms.definition: The POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION and POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBERSHIP are used to encode a hierarchy of classifications to index and find different types of POINT OF INTEREST. For example, Educational Building -#gt; School -#gt; Primary School , or Cultural Attraction -#gt; Museum -#gt; Art Museum . POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBERSHIP does not have to be disjoint, i.e. the same category may appear in more than one classification. Notes: Identifier of POINT OF INTEREST CLASSIFICATION MEMBERSHIP.

terms.label: NT Path & Navigation Path MODEL::PATH LINK
terms.definition: A link within a PLACE of or between two PLACEs (that is STOP PLACEs, ACCESS SPACEs or QUAYs,BOARDING POSITIONs,, POINTs OF INTEREST etc or PATH JUNCTIONs) that represents a step in a possible route for pedestrians, cyclists or other out-of-vehicle passengers within or between a PLACE. NOTE: It is possible but not mandatory that a PATH LINK projects onto a more detailed set of infrastructure or mapping links that plot the spatial course, allowing it to be represented on maps and to tracking systems. Notes: Access feature type associated with PATH LINK. Notes: Whether all areas of component are accessible in a Wheelchair. Notes: Allowed direction of use of PATH LINK. Notes: Direction heading to show for PATH LINK when travelling in its TO / FROM sense Notes: Nature of covering of PATH LINK. Notes: Description of PATH LINK. Notes: Whether element is within a gated area. Notes: Identifier of a PATH LINK. Notes: How element is lit. Notes: Maximum number of passengers that can use a PATH LINK. Notes: Number of steps involved in using a PATH LINK. Notes: Type of passage traversed by PATH LINK, if any. This provides a more precis description of Access Feature type. Notes: Number of people that can be in component at a time. Notes: Whether the link is available for PUBLIC use. Notes: Description of a towards direction. Notes: Transition for with PATH LINK: up, down, level.

terms.label: NT Path & Navigation Path MODEL::PATH LINK END
terms.definition: Beginning or end SITE for a PATH LINK. May be linked to a specific LEVEL of the SITE. Notes: Whether all areas of component are accessible in a Wheelchair. Notes: Whether element is covered or outdoors. Notes: Whether element is within a gated area. Notes: Identifier of a PATH JUNCTION. Notes: Label of a PATH JUNCTION. Notes: How element is lit. Notes: Number of people that can be in component at a time. Notes: Whether element can be used by the general public.

terms.label: NT Path & Navigation Path MODEL::PATH JUNCTION
terms.definition: A designated point, inside or outside of a STOP PLACE or POINT OF INTEREST, at which two or more PATH LINKs may connect or branch. Notes: Whether all areas of component are accessible in a Wheelchair. Notes: Whether element is covered or outdoors. Notes: Whether element is within a gated area. Notes: Identifier of a PATH JUNCTION. Notes: Label of a PATH JUNCTION. Notes: How element is lit. Notes: Number of people that can be in component at a time. Notes: Whether element can be used by the general public.

terms.label: NT Path & Navigation Path MODEL::NAVIGATION PATH
terms.definition: A designated path between two places. May include an ordered sequence of PATH LINKs. Notes: Type of an ACCESS Feature. Notes: ACCESSIBILITY ASSESSMENT associated with NAVIGATION PATH. Notes: Whether all areas of component are accessible in a Wheelchair. Notes: Nature of covering of NAVIGATION PATH. Notes: Origin end of NAVIGATION PATH. Only needed if detailed PATH LINKs are not given. Notes: Whether element is within a gated area. Notes: Identifier of a NAVIGATION PATH. Notes: How element is lit. Notes: Type of NAVIGATION PATH. Notes: Number of people that can be in component at a time. Notes: Whether PATH is for PUBLIC use. Notes: Destination end of NAVIGATION PATH. Only needed if detailed PATH LINKs are not given. Notes: Time it takes to traverse a NAVIGATION PATH. May be derived from summing individual PATH LINK durations.

terms.label: NT Path & Navigation Path MODEL::PLACE IN SEQUENCE
terms.definition: Point traversed by a NAVIGATION PATH in sequence, connected by a PATH LINK to the next point. May be a Place, PATH JUNCTION or POINT. Notes: Identifier of SITE POINT IN SEQUENCE. Notes: Label of SITE POINT IN SEQUENCE. Notes: Order of SITE POINT IN SEQUENCE within NAVIGATION PATH..

terms.label: NT Path & Navigation Path MODEL::PATH LINK IN SEQUENCE
terms.definition: A step of a NAVIGATION PATH indicating traversal of a particular PATH LINK as part of a recommended route. The same PATH LINK may occur in different sequences in different NAVIGATION PATHs. Notes: Permitted Direction of travel. Notes: Heading instruction relative to point declared 'left', 'right' onwards, etc. Notes: Identifier of PATH LINK IN SEQUENCE. Notes: Label of PATH LINK IN SEQUENCE. Notes: Order of PATH LINK IN SEQUENCE. within LINK SEQUENCE.

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::CHECK CONSTRAINT
terms.definition: Characteristics of a process that takes place at a SITE COMPONENT, such as check-in, security screening, ticket control or immigration, that may potentially incur a time penalty that should be allowed for when journey planning. Notes: Access feature associated with CHECK CONSTRAINT. Notes: Direction in which CHECK CONSTRAINT applies: forwards, back or both. For CHECK CONSTRAINT associated with links, corresponds to direction of link. For CHECK CONSTRAINT associated with ENTRANCEs corresponds to direction from outside SITE to inside SITE. Notes: Identifier of CHECK CONSTRAINT. Notes: Name of CHECK CONSTRAINT. Notes: Order of CHECK CONSTRAINT.

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::CHECK CONSTRAINT DELAY
terms.definition: Time penalty associated with a CHECK CONSTRAINT. Notes: Average duration of delay of CHECK CONSTRAINT DELAY. Notes: Identifier of CHECK CONSTRAINT DELAY. Notes: Maximum expected duration of delay of CHECK CONSTRAINT DELAY. Notes: Minimum expected duration of delay of CHECK CONSTRAINT DELAY.

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::CHECK CONSTRAINT THROUGHPUT
terms.definition: Throughput of a CHECK CONSTRAINT: the number of passengers who can pass through it in a specified interval. Notes: Average number of passengers for CHECK CONSTRAINT THROUGHPUT. Notes: Identifier of CHECK CONSTRAINT THROUGHPUT. Notes: Maximum number of passengers for CHECK CONSTRAINT THROUGHPUT. Notes: Identifier of PERIOD for CHECK CONSTRAINT THROUGHPUT. Notes: Maximum number of wheelchair passengers for CHECK CONSTRAINT THROUGHPUT.

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::TYPE OF ACCESS FEATURE
terms.definition: A Classification of ACCESS FEATURE for CHECK CONSTRAINT (e.g. barrier, narrow entrance, confined space, queue management, etc.) Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ACCESS FEATURE.

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::TYPE OF CHECK CONSTRAINT
terms.definition: A classification of CHECK CONSTRAINT (e.g. ticket collection, ticket purchase, baggage check-in, incoming customs, outgoing customs, tax refunds, etc.) Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF CHECK CONSTRAINT

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::TYPE OF CONGESTION
terms.definition: A typology of congestions resulting from CHECK CONSTRAINT (e.g. no waiting, queue, crowding, full). Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF CONGESTION.

terms.label: NT Check Constraint MODEL::TYPE OF SERVICE NATURE
terms.definition: A classification for service available for a CHECK CONSTRAINT (e.g. self-service machine, counter service). Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF SERVICE NATURE.

terms.label: NT Vehicle Stopping MODEL::VEHICLE QUAY ALIGNMENT
terms.definition: The alignment of a particular QUAY with a vehicle as the result of positioning a VEHICLE at a particular VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE QUAY ALIGNMENT.

terms.label: NT Vehicle Stopping MODEL::VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE
terms.definition: A place on the vehicle track where vehicles stop in order for passengers to board or alight from a vehicle. A vehicle track is located on the respective INFRASTUCTURE LINK for the MODE (RAILWAY ELEMENT of rail network, ROAD ELEMENT of road network, etc). A VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE may be served by one or more QUAYs. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE.

terms.label: NT Vehicle Stopping MODEL::VEHICLE STOPPING POSITION
terms.definition: The stopping position of a vehicle or one of its components as a location. May be specified as a ZONE corresponding to the bounding polygon of the vehicle, or one or more POINTs corresponding to parts of the vehicle such as a door. If given as a single point, indicates the position for the door relative to an indicated side of the vehicle. Notes: Bearing of Position relative to North. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE STOPPING POSITION.

terms.label: NT Vehicle Stopping MODEL::TYPE OF RELATION TO VEHICLE
terms.definition: A classification of the way a VEHICLE STOPPING POSITION is used (e.g. front left, front right, back left, back right, driver left, driver right). Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF RELATION TO VEHICLE.

terms.label: NT Vehicle Stopping MODEL::VEHICLE POSITION ALIGNMENT
terms.definition: The alignment of a particular BOARDING POSITION with the entrance of a VEHICLE as the result of positioning the VEHICLE at a particular VEHICLE STOPPING PLACE. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE POSITION ALIGNMENT.

terms.label: NT Journey Pattern MODEL::JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: An ordered list of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs and TIMING POINTs on a single ROUTE, describing the pattern of working for public transport vehicles.A JOURNEY PATTERN may pass through the same POINT more than once. The first point of a JOURNEY PATTERN is the origin. The last point is the destination. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Journey Pattern MODEL::DEAD RUN PATTERN
terms.definition: A JOURNEY PATTERN to be used for DEAD RUNs. Notes: Identifier of DEAD RUN JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Journey Pattern MODEL::POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: A SCHEDULED STOP POINT or TIMING POINT in a JOURNEY PATTERN with its order in that JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Identifier of POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Journey Pattern MODEL::TIMING LINK IN JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: The position of a TIMING LINK in a JOURNEY PATTERN. This entity is needed if a TIMING LINK is repeated in the same JOURNEY PATTERN, and separate information is to be stored about each iteration of the TIMING LINK. Notes: Identifier of TIMING LINK IN JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Journey Pattern MODEL::TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: A POINT in a JOURNEY PATTERN which is a TIMING POINT. Notes: Identifier of TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Whether TIMING POINT is a wait point.

terms.label: NT Journey Pattern MODEL::TYPE OF JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: A classification of JOURNEY PATTERNs used to distinguish other categories of JOURNEY PATTERN than SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN and DEAD RUN PATTERN. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Name of TYPE OF JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Notice Assignment MODEL::NOTICE ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The assignment of a NOTICE showing an exception in a JOURNEY PATTERN, a COMMON SECTION, or a VEHICLE JOURNEY, possibly specifying at which POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN the validity of the NOTICE starts and ends respectively. Notes: Whether NOTICE is shown to public. Notes: Identifier of NOTICE ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Mark associated with NOTICE. Notes: URL to fetch icon for Mark associated with NOTICE.

terms.label: NT Passenger Information Display Assignment MODEL::DISPLAY ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The assignment of one SCHEDULED STOP POINT and one JOURNEY PATTERN to a PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT specifying that information on the SCHEDULED STOP POINT and the JOURNEY PATTERN will be provided (e.g. displayed, printed). Notes: Type Of DISPLAY ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Relative pririty of assignment Notes: Identifier of DISPLAY ASSIGNMENT. Notes: The number of journeys of a given LINE to show. Notes: MODE for which Data is to be shown on LOGICAL DISPLAY

terms.label: NT Passenger Information Display Assignment MODEL::LOGICAL DISPLAY
terms.definition: A set of data that can be assembled for assignment to a physical PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT or to a logical channel such as web or media. It is independent of any physical embodiment. A LOGICAL DISPLAY may have a set of DISPLAY ASSIGNMENTS each of which associates a JOURNEY PATTERN whose journeys are to be shown at the LOGICAL DISPLAY. It may also be associated with a SCHEDULED STOP POINT. A LOGICAL DISPLAY corresponds to a SIRI STOP MONITORING point. Notes: Description of LOGICAL DISPLAY. Notes: Identifier of LOGICAL DISPLAY. Notes: Name of LOGICAL DISPLAY.

terms.label: NT Passenger Information Display Assignment MODEL::PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT
terms.definition: A public transport information piece of equipment, as for instance terminals (on street, at information desks, telematic, ...) or printed material (leaflets displayed at stops, booklets, ...). Notes: Types of Accessibility Info available on PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT. Notes: URL for PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT. Notes: Description of PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT. Notes: Identifier of PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT. Notes: Name of PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT. Notes: Types of Passenger Travel Info available.

terms.label: NT Passenger Information Display Assignment MODEL::TYPE OF PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT
terms.definition: A classification for PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT (e.g. next stop indicator, stop announcements, passenger information facility). Notes: Classification of PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PASSENGER INFORMATION EQUIPMENT.

terms.label: NT Timing Pattern MODEL::TIMING LINK
terms.definition: An ordered pair of TIMING POINTs for which run times may be recorded. Notes: Identifier of a TIMING LINK.

terms.label: NT Timing Pattern MODEL::TIMING PATTERN
terms.definition: The subset of a JOURNEY PATTERN made up only of TIMING POINTs IN JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Identifier of TIMING PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Timing Pattern MODEL::TIMING POINT
terms.definition: A POINT against which the timing information necessary to build schedules may be recorded. Notes: Default Wait time to use for TIMING PATTERNs that use TIMING POINT. TIME DEMAND TYPE specific values may be specified using a TIME DEMAND TYPE TIMING. Notes: Category of a TIMING POINT. Notes: Whether TIMING POINT is usable in a FLEXIBLE JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of a TIMING POINT. Notes: Timing status of POINT; principle, secondary, other.

terms.label: NT Timing Pattern MODEL::GROUP OF TIMING LINKS
terms.definition: A set of TIMING LINKs grouped together according to the similarity of TIME BANDs which are relevant to them. There may be a GROUP OF TIMING LINKS which covers all TIMING LINKs, for use when different GROUPs OF TIMING LINKS are not needed. Notes: Description of GROUP OF TIMING LINKS. Notes: Identifier of GROUP OF TIMING LINKs.

terms.label: NT Service Connection MODEL::DEFAULT CONNECTION
terms.definition: The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to change from one public transport vehicle to another to continue the trip. It specifies default times to be used to change from one mode of transport to another at an area or national level as specified by a TOPOGRAPHIC PLACE, STOP AREA or SITE ELEMENT. It may be restricted to a specific MODE or OPERATOR or only apply in a particular direction of transfer, e.g. bus to rail may have a different time for rail to bus. Notes: Identifier of DEFAULT TRANSFER.

terms.label: NT Service Connection MODEL::DEFAULT CONNECTION END
terms.definition: One end of a DEFAULT CONNECTION. Notes: Identifier of DEFAULT CONNECTION END.

terms.label: NT Service Connection MODEL::SITE CONNECTION
terms.definition: The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to change from one public transport vehicle to another to continue the trip, determined by physical locations, such as SITEs and/or its components and/or ENTRANCEs, in particular STOP PLACEs and/or its components. Different times may be necessary to cover the resulting distance, depending on the kind of passenger. Notes: Identifier of SITE CONNECTION link.

terms.label: NT Service Connection MODEL::SITE CONNECTION END
terms.definition: One end of a SITE CONNECTION. Notes: Identifier of SITE CONNECTION END.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::SCHEDULED STOP POINT
terms.definition: A POINT where passengers can board or alight from vehicles. Notes: Whether STOP POINT can be considered as being at the centre of a TOPOGRAPHIC PLACE. Default is false. Notes: Heading of stop relative to street. Degrees from North. This should be considered as a derived value that can be used for presentation purposes when information about the physical stop is not available. . The definitive value is the compass bearing found on the QUAY (ie physical stop) to which a SCHEDULED STOP POINT is assigned. Notes: Description of SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: Default for whether stop may be used for alighting. May be overridden on specific services. Notes: Default for whether stop may be used for boarding . May be overridden on specific services. Notes: Identifier of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: Label of SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: Default for whether stop is a request stop. May be overridden in JOURNEY PATTERNs. Notes: Short Name of SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: URL associated with SCHEDULED STOP POINT.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::SERVICE LINK
terms.definition: A LINK between an ordered pair of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs. Notes: Identifier of a SERVICE LINK. Notes: Mode of transport for which SERVICE LINK applies.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::SERVICE PATTERN
terms.definition: The subset of a JOURNEY PATTERN made up only of STOP POINTs IN JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Identifier of a SERVICE PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: The JOURNEY PATTERN for a (passenger carrying) SERVICE JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::STOP AREA
terms.definition: A group of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs close to each other. Notes: Identifier of a STOP AREA. Notes: Name of STOP AREA. Notes: PUBLIC CODE for a STOP AREA.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::STOP POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: A POINT in a JOURNEY PATTERN which is a SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: Whether DESTINATION DISPLAY changes at this point. Notes: Whether SERVICE REQUIREMENTs change at this point. Notes: Whether stop may be used for alighting. Notes: Whether stop may be used for boarding. Notes: Identifier of a STOP POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Whether the stop is a Request Stop. Notes: Nature of use of stop, e.g. access, interchange only, or pass through. Default is Access.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::CONNECTION
terms.definition: The physical (spatial) possibility for a passenger to change from one public transport vehicle to another to continue the trip, determined by two SCHEDULED STOP POINTs. Different times may be necessary to cover the link between these points, depending on the kind of passenger. Notes: Identifier of a CONNECTION. Notes: Whether connecting at this stop passengers may only transfer. If true, then they may not enter or exit at the station.

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::CONNECTION END
terms.definition: One end of a CONNECTION. Notes: Identifier of CONNECTION END;

terms.label: NT Service Pattern MODEL::TYPE OF STOP POINT
terms.definition: A classification of SCHEDULED STOP POINTs, used for instance to characterize the equipment to be installed at stops (post, shelter, seats, etc.). Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF STOP POINT.

terms.label: NT Common Section MODEL::COMMON SECTION
terms.definition: A part of a public transport network where the ROUTEs of several JOURNEY PATTERNs are going in parallel and where the synchronisation of SERVICE JOURNEYs may be planned and controlled with respect to commonly used LINKs and SCHEDULED STOP POINTs. COMMON SECTIONs are defined arbitrarily and need not cover the total lengths of topologically bundled sections. Notes: Description of COMMON SECTION. Notes: Identifier of COMMON SECTION

terms.label: NT Routing Constraint MODEL::ROUTING CONSTRAINT ZONE
terms.definition: A ZONE defining a ROUTING CONSTRAINT. The ZONE may be defined by its contained SCHEDULED STOP POINTS or by its boundary points. Examples of routing constraints are : "If you board in this ZONE, you can't alight in the same ZONE". Notes: Identifier of ROUTING CONSTRAINT. Notes: How zone may be used.

terms.label: NT Routing Constraint MODEL::SERVICE EXCLUSION
terms.definition: A constraint expressing the fact that the service, on a specific JOURNEY PATTERN (usually a flexible transport service JOURNEY PATTERN) cannot operate when another (regular) service operates. This may occur only on a subpart of the JOURNEY PATTERN, or only on one or some specific SCHEDULED STOP POINTS. Notes: Description of SERVICE EXCLUSION. Notes: Identifier of SERVICE EXCLUSION. Notes: Name of SERVICE EXCLUSION.

terms.label: NT Routing Constraint MODEL::TRANSFER RESTRICTION
terms.definition: A constraint that can be applied on a CONNECTION or INTERCHANGE between two SCHEDULED STOP POINT, preventing or forbidding the passenger to use it. Notes: Whether TRANSFER can be traversed in both directions Notes: Description of SERVICE EXCLUSION. Notes: Identifier of TRANSFER RESTRICTION. Notes: Name of SERVICE EXCLUSION. Notes: Type of constraint applying to restriction.

terms.label: NT Time Demand Type MODEL::TIME DEMAND TYPE
terms.definition: An indicator of traffic conditions or other factors which may affect vehicle run or wait times. It may be entered directly by the scheduler or defined by the use of TIME BANDs. Notes: Description of TIME DEMAND TYPE. Notes: Identifier of TIME DEMAND TYPE. Notes: Name of TIME DEMAND TYPE.

terms.label: NT Time Demand Type MODEL::TIME DEMAND TYPE ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The assignment of a TIME DEMAND TYPE to a TIME BAND depending on the DAY TYPE and GROUP OF TIMING LINKS. Notes: Identifier of TIME DEMAND TYPE ASSIGNMENT.

terms.definition: Diagram Description This diagram is mainly extracted from IFOPT and represents the link between the logical stop point i.e. the ScheduledStopPoint(i.e. the Transmodel StopPoint) and the physical stop points (IFOPT StopPlaceComponent).

terms.definition: NT Stop Assignment MODEL : Public Package Created: 03/12/2009 12:02:07 Modified: 14/03/2018 22:44:52 Project: Author: NeTEx Version: 1.0 Phase: 1.0 Status: Validated Complexity: Easy Difficulty: Priority: Multiplicity: Advanced: UUID: {5476DA53-2EDB-4e59-85DD-ACC50197B538} Appears In:

terms.label: NT Stop Assignment MODEL::STOP ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The allocation of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (i.e. a SCHEDULED STOP POINT of a SERVICE PATTERN or JOURNEY PATTERN) to a specific STOP PLACE, for either a SERVICE JOURNEY or VEHICLE SERVICE. Notes: Whether STOP ASSIGNMENT allows alighting at the stop. Notes: Whether STOP ASSIGNMENT allows boarding at the stop. Notes: Identifier of a STOP ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Private code for element. Notes: Type of STOP ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: NT Stop Assignment MODEL::PASSENGER STOP ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The allocation of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (i.e. a SCHEDULED STOP POINT of a SERVICE PATTERN or JOURNEY PATTERN) to a specific STOP PLACE for a SERVICE JOURNEY, and also possibly a QUAY and BOARDING POSITION. Notes: Identifier of PASSENGER STOP ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: NT Stop Assignment MODEL::DYNAMIC STOP ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The dynamic association of a SCHEDULED STOP POINT (i.e. a SCHEDULED STOP POINT of a SERVICE PATTERN or JOURNEY PATTERN) with the next available STOP PLACE, QUAY or BOARDING POSITION within a STOP PLACE. Notes: Identifier of DYNAMIC STOP ASSIGNMENT

terms.definition: The association of a TRAIN COMPONENT at a SCHEDULED STOP POINT with a specific STOP PLACE and also possibly a QUAY and BOARDING POSITION. Notes: A specific ENTRANCE to the VEHICLE. E.g. Front, rear Notes: Identifier of TRAIN STOP ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Relative position of TRAIN ELEMENT.
