terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::TYPE OF PRODUCT CATEGORY
terms.definition: A classification for VEHICLE JOURNEYs to express some common properties of journeys for marketing and fare products Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PRODUCT CATEGORY.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::JOURNEY
terms.definition: Common properties of VEHICLE JOURNEYs and SPECIAL SERVICEs, e.g. their link to accounting characteristics. Notes: Vehicle Mode of JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY. Notes: Whether the journey is monitored with real-time tracking & predictions. Notes: Normal Primary Transport mode of JOURNEY Notes: Normal Primary Transport submode of JOURNEY

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::VEHICLE JOURNEY
terms.definition: The planned movement of a public transport vehicle on a DAY TYPE from the start point to the end point of a JOURNEY PATTERN on a specified ROUTE. Notes: Departure time of VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Duration of VEHICLE JOURNEY.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::DEAD RUN
terms.definition: A non-service VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Type of Dead Run. Notes: Type of DIRECTION. Notes: Identifier of DEAD RUN.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::TEMPLATE VEHICLE JOURNEY
terms.definition: A repeating VEHICLE JOURNEY for which a frequency has been specified, either as a HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP (e.g. every 20 minutes) or a RHYTHMICAL JOURNEY GROUP (e.g. at 15, 27 and 40 minutes past the hour). It may thus represent multiple journeys. Notes: Identifier of TEMPLATE VEHICLE JOURNEY.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::TRAIN NUMBER
terms.definition: Specification of codes assigned to particular VEHICLE JOURNEYs when operated by TRAINs or COMPOUND TRAINs according to a functional purpose (passenger information, operation follow-up, etc) Notes: Description of TRAIN NUMBER. Notes: TRAIN NUMBER to use for advertisement to public if different from ID. Notes: TRAIN NUMBER to use for advertisement to public, if different from ID. Notes: Identifier of TRAIN NUMBER.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey MODEL::TYPE OF SERVICE
terms.definition: A classification for VEHICLE JOURNEYs and SPECIAL SERVICEs to express some common properties of journeys to be taken into account in the scheduling and/or operations control process. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF SERVICE.

terms.label: TI Flexible Service MODEL::FLEXIBLE SERVICE PROPERTIES
terms.definition: Additional characteristics of flexible service. A service may be partly fixed, partly flexible. Notes: Whether cancellation is always possible (meaning the Operator can decided to cancel a journey, usually because there are not enough passenger, or they are too busy to run the service.) Notes: Whether time of service may be moved (usually a passing time update to optimise the service if there are not enough passenger, or they are too busy to run the service.) Notes: Identifier of FLEXIBLE SERVICE PROPERTIES.

terms.label: TI Flexible Service MODEL::TYPE OF FLEXIBLE SERVICE
terms.definition: A typology of flexible services: Virtual line service Flexible service with main route Corridor service Fixed stop area-wide flexible service Free area-wide flexible service Mixed types of flexible service (not at POINT level) The type of flexibility can be defined at JOURNEY PATTERN level or at POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN level in case of mixed types of flexible service inside the same JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF FLEXIBLE SERVICE.

terms.label: TI Journey Timing MODEL::JOURNEY TIMING
terms.definition: A time-related information referring to journey timing whose value depends on the time of use and so can be associated with a TIME DEMAND TYPE, TIME BAND or OPERATIONAL CONTEXT. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY DEMAND. Notes: Description of JOURNEY TIMING. Notes: TRANSPORT MODE of JOURNEY TIMING.

terms.label: TI Journey Timing MODEL::JOURNEY HEADWAY
terms.definition: Headway interval information that is available for all the VEHICLE JOURNEYs running on the JOURNEY PATTERN for a given TIME DEMAND TYPE, at a given TIMING POINT. This is a default value that can be superseded by VEHICLE JOURNEY HEADWAY. This information must be consistent with HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP if available (HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP being a more detailed way of describing headway services). Notes: Set of HEADWAY INTERVALs describing frequency of JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY HEADWAY.

terms.label: TI Journey Timing MODEL::JOURNEY LAYOVER
terms.definition: Time allowance at the end of each journey to allow for delays and for other purposes. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY LAYOVER. Notes: Time spent at JOURNEY LAYOVER.

terms.label: TI Journey Timing MODEL::JOURNEY RUN TIME
terms.definition: The time taken to traverse a TIMING LINK in a particular JOURNEY PATTERN, for a specified TIME DEMAND TYPE. If it exists, it will override the DEFAULT SERVICE JOURNEY RUN TIME and DEFAULT DEAD RUN RUN TIME. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY RUN TIME. Notes: Run time of JOURNEY RUN TIME.

terms.label: TI Journey Timing MODEL::JOURNEY WAIT TIME
terms.definition: The time a vehicle has to wait at a specific TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN, for a specified TIME DEMAND TYPE.This wait time can be superseded by a VEHICLE JOURNEY WAIT TIME. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY WAIT TIME. Notes: Wait time of JOURNEY WAIT TIME.

terms.label: TI Service Journey MODEL::SERVICE JOURNEY
terms.definition: A passenger carrying VEHICLE JOURNEY for one specified DAY TYPE. The pattern of working is in principle defined by a SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Type of DIRECTION. Notes: When this journey should be visible to public in Dynamic channels. Notes: Identifier of SERVICE JOURNEY. Notes: Whether this journey should be visible to public in Print channels. Notes: Status to journey - planned, cancelled, etc.

terms.label: TI Service Journey MODEL::SPECIAL SERVICE
terms.definition: A work of a vehicle that is not planned in a classical way, i.e. that is generally not based on VEHICLE JOURNEYs using JOURNEY PATTERNs. It involves specific characteristics (such as specific access rights) and/or may be operated under specific circumstances. Notes: Client for SPECIAL SERVICE. Notes: Departure time of VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: When this journey should be visible to public in Dynamic channels. Notes: Identifier of SPECIAL SERVICE. Notes: Duration of VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Whether this journey should be visible to public in Print channels.

terms.label: TI Service Journey MODEL::GROUP OF SERVICES
terms.definition: A group of SERVICEs, often known to its users by a name or a number. Notes: Type of DIRECTION. Notes: Identifier of GROUP OF SERVICEs.

terms.label: TI Service Journey MODEL::TEMPLATE SERVICE JOURNEY
terms.definition: A passenger carrying TEMPLATE SERVICE JOURNEY. As TEMPLATE SERVICE JOURNEY, it may represent multiple journeys. Notes: Identifier of TEMPLATE SERVICE JOURNEY.

terms.label: TI JT Time Demand Times MODEL

terms.label: TI Time Demand Times MODEL

terms.label: TI Time Demand Times MODEL::DEFAULT SERVICE JOURNEY RUN TIME
terms.definition: The default time taken by a vehicle to traverse a TIMING LINK during a SERVICE JOURNEY, for a specified TIME DEMAND TYPE. This time may be superseded by the JOURNEY PATTERN RUN TIME or VEHICLE JOURNEY RUN TIME if these exist. Notes: Identifier of DEFAULT SERVICE JOURNEY RUN TIME. Notes: Run time as a duration.

terms.label: TI Time Demand Times MODEL::DEFAULT DEAD RUN RUN TIME
terms.definition: The time taken to traverse a TIMING LINK during a DEAD RUN, for a specified TIME DEMAND TYPE. This time may be superseded by the JOURNEY PATTERN RUN TIME or VEHICLE JOURNEY RUN TIME if these exist. Notes: Identifier of DEFAULT DEAD RUN RUN TIME. Notes: Time to make a DEAD RUN.

terms.label: TI Journey Pattern Times MODEL::JOURNEY PATTERN WAIT TIME
terms.definition: The time a vehicle has to wait at a specific TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN, for a specified TIME DEMAND TYPE. This wait time can be superseded by a VEHICLE JOURNEY WAIT TIME. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PATTERN WAIT TIME.

terms.label: TI Journey Pattern Times MODEL::JOURNEY PATTERN RUN TIME
terms.definition: The time taken to traverse a TIMING LINK in a particular JOURNEY PATTERN, for a specified TIME DEMAND TYPE. If it exists, it will override the DEFAULT SERVICE JOURNEY RUN TIME and DEFAULT DEAD RUN RUN TIME. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PATTERN RUN TIME.

terms.label: TI Journey Pattern Times MODEL::JOURNEY PATTERN LAYOVER
terms.definition: Time allowance at the end of each journey on a specified JOURNEY PATTERN, to allow for delays and for other purposes. This layover supersedes any global layover and may be superseded by a specific VEHICLE JOURNEY LAYOVER. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PATTERN LAYOVER.

terms.label: TI Journey Pattern Times MODEL::JOURNEY PATTERN HEADWAY
terms.definition: Headway interval information that is available for all the VEHICLE JOURNEYs running on the JOURNEY PATTERN. This is a default value that can be superseded by the VEHICLE JOURNEY HEADWAY on a specific journey. This information must be consistent with HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP if available (HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP being a more detailed way of describing headway services). Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PATTERN HEADWAY.

terms.label: TI Journey Pattern Times MODEL::TURNAROUND TIME LIMIT
terms.definition: The maximum time for which a vehicle may be scheduled to wait at a particular TIMING POINT (often included in a TURN STATION) without being returned to a PARKING POINT. A minimum time for a vehicle to turn its direction may also be recorded. This may be superseded by a DEAD RUN. Notes: Identifier of TURNAROUND TIME LIMIT Notes: Maximum time deeded for turnaround Notes: Minimum time deeded for turnaround

terms.label: TI Journey Pattern Times MODEL::VEHICLE TYPE PREFERENCE
terms.definition: The preference for the use of a particular VEHICLE TYPE for a SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN, depending on the DAY TYPE and TIME DEMAND TYPE. The rank of preferences must be recorded. Different VEHICLE TYPEs may be given the same rank. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE TYPE PREFERENCE. Notes: Ranking of VEHICLE TYPE PREFERENCE.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::HEADWAY INTERVAL
terms.definition: A time interval or a duration defining a headway period and characterizing HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP (e.g. every 10 min, every 4-6 min). Notes: Identifier of HEADWAY INTERVAL. Notes: Maximum Headway interval. Notes: Minimum Headway interval. Notes: Scheduled Headway interval.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::VEHICLE JOURNEY LAYOVER
terms.definition: A time allowance at the end of a specified VEHICLE JOURNEY. This time supersedes any global layover or JOURNEY PATTERN LAYOVER. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE JOURNEY LAYOVER.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::VEHICLE JOURNEY RUN TIME
terms.definition: The time taken to traverse a specified TIMING LINK IN JOURNEY PATTERN on a specified VEHICLE JOURNEY. This gives the most detailed control over times and overrides the DEFAULT SERVICE JOURNEY RUN TIME and JOURNEY PATTERN RUN TIME and the DEFAULT DEAD RUN RUN TIME. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE JOURNEY RUN TIME.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::VEHICLE JOURNEY WAIT TIME
terms.definition: The time for a vehicle to wait at a particular TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN on a specified VEHICLE JOURNEY. This wait time will override the JOURNEY PATTERN WAIT TIME. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE JOURNEY WAIT TIME.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::JOURNEY FREQUENCY GROUP
terms.definition: A group of JOURNEYs defined in order to describe special behaviour like frequency based services or rhythmical services (runs all xxh10, xxh25 and xxh45... for example; this is especially useful for passenger information). Notes: Offset of end time day from start time. Notes: Time of first departure in Group. Notes: Identifier of FREQUENCY GROUP. Notes: Time of last departure in Group.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP
terms.definition: A group of VEHICLE JOURNEYs following the same JOURNEY PATTERN having the same HEADWAY INTERVAL between a specified start and end time (for example, every 10 min). This is especially useful for passenger information. Notes: How Headway is to displayed to passengers. Notes: Identifier of HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::RHYTHMICAL JOURNEY GROUP
terms.definition: A group of VEHICLE JOURNEYS following the same JOURNEY PATTERN having the same "rhythm" every hour (for example runs at xxh10, xxh25 and xxh45... ) between a specified start and end time. Notes: Identifier of RHYTHMICAL JOURNEY GROUP.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Journey Times MODEL::VEHICLE JOURNEY HEADWAY
terms.definition: Headway interval information that is available for a VEHICLE JOURNEY (to be understood as the delay between the previous and the next VEHICLE JOURNEY). This information must be consistent with HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP if available (HEADWAY JOURNEY GROUP being a more detailed way of describing headway services). Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE JOURNEY HEADWAY.

terms.label: TI Interchange MODEL::JOURNEY MEETING
terms.definition: A time constraint for one or several SERVICE JOURNEYs fixing interchanges between them and/or an external event (e.g. arrival or departure of a feeder line, opening time of the theatre, etc.). Notes: Description of JOURNEY MEETING. Notes: Latest time at which MEETING can take place. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY MEETING. Notes: Earliest time at which MEETING can take place. Notes: Reason for JOURNEY MEETING.

terms.label: TI Interchange MODEL::DEFAULT INTERCHANGE
terms.definition: A quality parameter fixing the acceptable duration (standard and maximum) for an INTERCHANGE to be planned between two SCHEDULED STOP POINTs. This parameter will be used to control whether any two VEHICLE JOURNEYs serving those points may be in connection. Notes: Description of JOURNEY MEETING. Notes: Identifier of DEFAULT INTERCHANGE. Notes: Maximum wait time for DEFAULT INTERCHANGE. Notes: Standard wait time for DEFAULT INTERCHANGE.

terms.label: TI Interchange MODEL::INTERCHANGE
terms.definition: The scheduled possibility for transfer of passengers at the same or different SCHEDULED STOP POINTs. Notes: Whether INTERCHANGE is controlled. Notes: Whether INTERCHANGE is advertised as guaranteed. Notes: Whether INTERCHANGE involves crossing a national border. Notes: Description of INTERCHANGE. Notes: Maximum wait time a vehicle may wait for a connecting vehicle beyond the planned departure time. Notes: Whether INTERCHANGE is guaranteed, that is distributor services may be held in order to ensure the connection. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE. Notes: Name of INTERCHANGE. Notes: Whether INTERCHANGE is planned. Notes: Priority assigned to INTERCHANGE. Notes: Whether passengers can stay seated to make INTERCHANGE. Notes: Modes by which transfer at the interchange can be made.

terms.label: TI Interchange MODEL::SERVICE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE
terms.definition: The scheduled possibility for transfer of passengers between two SERVICE JOURNEYs at the same or different SCHEDULED STOP POINTs. Notes: Visit number of feeder journey (only needed if multiple visits). Notes: Identifier of SERVICE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE. Notes: Visit number of distributor journey (only needed if multiple visits).

terms.label: TI Interchange MODEL::SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN INTERCHANGE
terms.definition: A recognised/organised possibility for passengers to change public transport vehicles using two SCHEDULED STOP POINTs (which may be identical) on two particular SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERNs, including the maximum wait duration allowed and the standard to be aimed at. These may supersede the times given for the DEFAULT INTERCHANGE. Schedulers may use this entity for synchronisation of journeys. Notes: Identifier of SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN INTERCHANGE.

terms.label: TI Interchange Rule MODEL::INTERCHANGE RULE
terms.definition: Conditions for considering JOURNEYs to meet or not to meet, specified indirectly: by a particular MODE, DIRECTION or LINE. Such conditions may alternatively be specified directly, indicating the corresponding services. In this case they are either a SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN INTERCHANGE or a SERVICE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE. Notes: Whether rule is to exclude interchanges of journeys that match the filter criteria. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE RULE. Notes: Maximum window for holding DISTRIBUTOR will wait. Notes: Relative priority of rule compared to other rules.

terms.label: TI Interchange Rule MODEL::INTERCHANGE RULE PARAMETER
terms.definition: Assignment of parameters characterising an INTERCHANGE RULE. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE RULE PARAMETER. Notes: Maximum interval for making interchange.

terms.label: TI Interchange Rule MODEL::INTERCHANGE RULE TIMING
terms.definition: Timings for an INTERCHANGE RULE for a given TIME DEMAND TYPE or TIME BAND. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE RULE TIMING.

terms.label: TI Coupled Journey MODEL::JOURNEY PART
terms.definition: A part of a VEHICLE JOURNEY created according to a specific functional purpose, for instance in situations when vehicle coupling or separating occurrs. Notes: Description of a JOURNEY PART. Notes: End time of a JOURNEY PART. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PART. Notes: Whether VEHICLE or TRAIN is operating forwards or backwards for the JOURNEY PART. terms.label: TI Coupled Journey MODEL::COUPLED JOURNEY
terms.definition: A complete journey operated by a coupled train, composed of two or more VEHICLE JOURNEYs remaining coupled together all along a JOURNEY PATTERN. A COUPLED JOURNEY may be viewed as a single VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Description of a JOURNEY PART. Notes: Identifier of COUPLED JOURNEY. Notes: Name of COUPLED JOURNEY.

terms.label: TI Coupled Journey MODEL::JOURNEY PART COUPLE
terms.definition: Two JOURNEY PARTs of different VEHICLE JOURNEYs served simultaneously by a train set up by coupling their single vehicles. Notes: Description of JOURNEY PART COUPLE. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY PART COUPLE. Notes: Order of JOURNEY PART COUPLE within JOURNEY.

terms.label: TI Coupled Journey MODEL::PURPOSE OF JOURNEY PARTITION
terms.definition: An operational purpose changing within a JOURNEY PATTERN and with this subdividing the SERVICE JOURNEY into JOURNEY PARTs. Notes: Identifier of PURPOSE OF JOURNEY PARTITION.

terms.label: TI Coupled Journey MODEL::TYPE OF COUPLING
terms.definition: A classification for COUPLING of BLOCK PARTs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF COUPLING.

terms.label: TI Passing Times MODEL ::DATED PASSING TIME
terms.definition: A PASSING TIME on a particular OPERATING DAY. Notes: Identifier of DATED PASSING TIME.

terms.label: TI Passing Times MODEL ::TARGET PASSING TIME
terms.definition: Time data about when a public transport vehicle should pass a particular POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN on a particular DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY, in order to match the latest valid plan. Notes: Intended Arrival time at TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN Notes: Intended Departure time at TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN Notes: Intended Passing time at TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN if vehicle does not stop Notes: Aimed waiting time at TIMING POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN Notes: Identifier of AIMED PASSING TIME.

terms.label: TI Passing Times MODEL ::PASSING TIME
terms.definition: Time data concerning public transport vehicles passing a particular POINT; e.g. arrival time, departure time, waiting time. Notes: Whether passengers can alight and reboard at TIMING POINT. Notes: Day offset of arrival time from day of start of journey. Notes: Day offset of departure time from day of start of journey. Notes: Identifier of TIMETABLED PASSING TIME.

terms.label: TI Passing Times MODEL ::TIMETABLED PASSING TIME

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::BLOCK
terms.definition: The work of a vehicle from the time it leaves a PARKING POINT after parking until its next return to park at a PARKING POINT. Any subsequent departure from a PARKING POINT after parking marks the start of a new BLOCK. The period of a BLOCK has to be covered by DUTies. Notes: Description of BLOCK. Notes: End time of BLOCK in principle this can be derived from the Start time of the last journey and the finishing duration. . Notes: Day offset of end time from start time Notes: How long needed to prepare to complete BLOCK. Notes: Identifier of BLOCK. Notes: Name of BLOCK. Notes: How long needed to prepare to run BLOCK. Notes: Start time of BLOCK in principle this can be derived from the Start time of the first journey and the preparation duration. . Notes: Day offset of start time from OPERATING DAY.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::BLOCK PART
terms.definition: Part of a BLOCK corresponding to the different JOURNEY PARTs of the VEHICLE JOURNEYs in a BLOCK. Notes: Description of BLOCK PART. Notes: Identifier of BLOCK PART. Notes: Description of COURSE OF JOURNEYs. Notes: Order of BLOCK PART within BLOCK

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::COMPOUND BLOCK
terms.definition: The work of a vehicle during the time it is coupled to another vehicle. Notes: Identifier of COMPOUND BLOCK. Notes: Name of COMPOUND BLOCK.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::COURSE OF JOURNEYS
terms.definition: A part of a BLOCK composed of consecutive VEHICLE JOURNEYs defined for the same DAY TYPE, all operated on the same LINE. Notes: Description of COURSE OF JOURNEYs. Notes: How long COURSE OF JOURNEY in BLOCK. Notes: Identifier of COURSE OF JOURNEY. Notes: Description of COURSE OF JOURNEYs. Notes: How long needed to prepare for COURSE OF JOURNEY in BLOCK. Notes: Day offset of start time from OPERATING DAY. Notes: Start time of COURSE OF JOURNEY in BLOCK.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::DATED BLOCK
terms.definition: The work of a vehicle on a particular OPERATING DAY from the time it leaves a PARKING POINT after parking until its next return to park at a PARKING POINT. Notes: Identifier of DATED BLOCK.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::NORMAL DATED BLOCK
terms.definition: A DATED BLOCK identical to a long-terms planned BLOCK, possibly updated according to short-term modifications decided by the control staff. Notes: Identifier of NORMAL DATED BLOCK.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::RELIEF OPPORTUNITY
terms.definition: A time in a BLOCK where a vehicle passes a RELIEF POINT. This opportunity may or may not be actually used for a relief. Notes: DESCRIPTION of RELIEF OPPORTUNITY. Notes: Identifier of RELIEF OPPORTUNITY. Notes: NAME of RELIEF OPPORTUNITY. Notes: TIME at which RELIEF OPPORTUNITY takes place.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::VEHICLE SERVICE
terms.definition: A workplan for a vehicle for a whole day, planned for a specific DAY TYPE. Notes: Description of VEHICLE SERVICE. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE SERVICE. Notes: Name of VEHICLE SERVICE.

terms.label: TI Vehicle Service MODEL::VEHICLE SERVICE PART
terms.definition: A part of a VEHICLE SERVICE composed of one or more BLOCKs and limited by periods spent at the GARAGE managing the vehicle in question. Notes: Description of VEHICLE SERVICE PART. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE SERVICE PART. Notes: Name of VEHICLE SERVICE PART.

terms.label: AC Generic Assignment::ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The association of one or more other assigned ENTITies with a primary ENTITY in order to describe some characteristic of the 'assigned to' ENTITY. The assignment may itself also have attributes. There may be multiple assignments applying to the same entity in which case an order and or VALIDITY CONDITIONs may apply in order to determine the current assignment to use. Notes: Identifier of ASSIGNMENT, Notes: Order in which assignments apply.

terms.definition: Describes Framework components already assumed by the Parts 1 2 and 3 models and that short be considered as part of the Core Transmodel Model. These should ultimately be migrated to a Part 1.

terms.label: TM AC Generic View MODEL
terms.definition: An ENTITY that aggregates the properties of other ENTITies, typically in order to simplify an implementation, but that does not itself add attributes or semantic content other than its own identity. VIEWs may have identifiers and may persist.

terms.label: AC Generic View MODEL
terms.definition: Describes a generic VIEW component, an ENTITY that aggregates the properties of other ENTITies, typically in order to simplify an implementation, but that does not itself add attributes or semantic content other than its own identity.

terms.label: AC Generic View MODEL::View
terms.definition: A VIEW assembles selected properties of one or more ENTITIEs into a separate named structure for read only use, usually to simplify an implementation. For example a CALL assembles POINT in JOURNEY PATTERN with PASSING TIMEs and other data describing a visit to an individual a STOP POINT by a SERVICE JOURNEY. A view may have a persistent identity and version, but all its attributes are derived through existing relationship to other ENTITIES and its data values can be considered as copies of the normalised data from which is derived. Notes: Identifier of VIEW,

terms.definition: Specifies through which channels a MESSAGE should be disseminated. Notes: Identifier of MESSAGE

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::MESSAGE
terms.definition: A communicated information . Notes: Identifier of MESSAGE

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::MESSAGE PART
terms.definition: A partial or complete information adapted for a specific type of usage and type of media. Notes: Identifier of MESSAGE PART.

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::MESSAGE PRIORITY
terms.definition: An arbitrary rating of how a MESSAGE ranks in relation to other potentially conflicting MESSAGEs when presentation bandwidth is limited. Notes: Identifier of MESSAGE PRIORITY.

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::TYPE OF MESSAGE
terms.definition: A classification of MESSAGEs. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF MESSAGE.

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::TYPE OF MESSAGE PART CONTENT
terms.definition: A classification of the content type e.g. Header, summary, detail etc. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF MESSAGE PART CONTENT

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::PT SCOPE
terms.definition: An extent consisting of public transport entities or combinations of entities such as OPERATORs, NETWORKs, LINEs, SCHEDULED STOP POINTs, STOP PLACEs, PLACEs, etc. Notes: Identifier of PT SCOPE.

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::PUBLICATION DECISION
terms.definition: An approval or disapproval regulating if a MESSAGE can be published in a certain PUBLICATION SCOPE. Notes: Identifier of PT SCOPE.

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::PUBLICATION SCOPE
terms.definition: An extent in which it is relevant to publish a MESSAGE expressed using entities such as LINEs, SCHEDULED STOP POINTs and VEHICLE JOURNEYs etc. Notes: Identifier of PUBLICATION SCOPE.

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::PUBLICATION WINDOW
terms.definition: A period during which the MESSAGE should be published. Notes: End time to display Message Notes: Identifier of PUBLICATION WINDOW. Notes: Start Time to display message

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::PUBLISHING ACTION
terms.definition: A guidance to processing options such as through which channels a MESSAGE should be disseminated. Notes: Identifier of PUBLISHING ACTION

terms.label: AC Message MODEL::TYPE OF AUDIENCE
terms.definition: A classification of the categories a MESSAGE is intended for, e.g. staff or passengers. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF AUDIENCE.

terms.label: AC Service Organisation Role MODEL::TRAVEL ORGANISATION ROLE
terms.definition: The role of an ORGANISATION in providing any kind of travel related service. Notes: Identifier of TRAVEL ORGANISATION ROLE

terms.label: AC Service Organisation Role MODEL::SERVICE OPERATOR ROLE
terms.definition: The role of an organisation that provides a service to the customer who uses a product - in particular the carrier role for public transport, but also possibly ancillary services such as catering, baggage handling, parking, etc. Notes: Identifier of SERVICE OPERATOR ROLE.

terms.label: AC Service Organisation Role MODEL::TRAVEL DOCUMENT CONTROLLING ORGANISATION ROLE
terms.definition: The role of organisation to providing the services of checking the validity of passenger's travel documents to check they have sufficient access rights for the journey that they are making Notes: Identifier of TRAVEL DOCUMENT CONTROLLING ORGANISATION ROLE

terms.label: AC Service Organisation Role MODEL::CUSTOMER SERVICE PROVIDER ROLE
terms.definition: The organisation role of providing "help line" and similar retail and fulfilment support facilities for CUSTOMERs, including replacement of stolen or damaged customer medium and assistance with the installation of applications. Notes: Identifier of CUSTOMER SERVICE PROVIDER ROLE .

terms.label: AC Employee Role MODEL::DRIVER ROLE
terms.definition: The DRIVER ROLE is to drive a VEHICLE. May also perform the ACCESS RIGHT CONTROLLER ROLE. Notes: Identifier of DRIVER ROLE..

terms.label: AC Employee Role MODEL::CONDUCTOR ROLE
terms.definition: The CONDUCTOR ROLE is to manage the on-board delivery of services and undertakes control and validation of TRAVEL DOCUMENTS. Notes: Identifier of CONDUCTOR ROLE..

terms.label: AC Employee Role MODEL::CUSTOMER SERVICE ROLE
terms.definition: The CUSTOMER SERVICE ROLE is to provide retail and assistance services through multiple channels, and works for a CUSTOMER SERVICE PROVIDER. Notes: Identifier of CUSTOMER SERVICE ROLE

terms.label: AC Employee Role MODEL::STATION EMPLOYEE ROLE
terms.definition: The STATION STAFF ROLE is to provide services at a station or other interchange. Notes: Identifier of STATION EMPLOYEE ROLE..

terms.label: AC Employee Role MODEL::TRAVEL DOCUMENT CONTROLLER ROLE
terms.definition: The EMPLOYEE ROLE to check travel documents. Often, but not necessarily, the same as a CONDUCTOR ROLE. Notes: Identifier of TRAVEL DOCUMENT CONTROLLER ROLE

terms.label: AC Administrative Organisation Role MODEL::REGISTRAR ROLE
terms.definition: The ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATION ROLE of coordinating the issue of unique registration codes for Organisations, Products, Travel Documents etc. etc. The Registrar , A function may issues unique identifiers directly or devise rules for generating unique identifiers Notes: Identifier of REGISTRAR ROLE

terms.label: AC Administrative Organisation Role MODEL::SECURITY MANAGER ROLE
terms.definition: The ADMINISTRATIVE ORGANISATION ROLE of establishing and coordinating a security policy across the provider organisations, and of the certifying and auditing of Organisations, Applications, etc for their conformance to the security policy. Notes: Identifier of SECURITY MANAGER ROLE

terms.label: AC Security List MODEL::SECURITY LIST
terms.definition: A list of items whose status is to be accepted or denied for a process such as purchase or validation. Notes: Description of BLACK LIST. Notes: Identifier of a SECURITY LIST. Notes: Name of BLACK LIST.

terms.label: AC Security List MODEL::BLACKLIST
terms.definition: A list of items (TRAVEL DOCUMENTs, CONTRACTs etc) the validity of which has been cancelled temporarily or permanently, for a specific reason like loss of the document, technical malfunction, no credit on bank account, offences committed by the customer, etc. Notes: Identifier of a BLACKLIST.

terms.label: AC Security List MODEL::WHITELIST
terms.definition: A list of items ( TRAVEL DOCUMENTs, CONTRACTs, etc) explicitly approved for processing. Notes: Identifier of a WHITE LIST.

terms.label: AC Security List MODEL::SECURITY LISTING
terms.definition: The presence of an identified Entity on a SECURITY LIST.. Notes: Identifier of a SECURITY LISTING

terms.label: AC Security List MODEL::SECURITY LISTABLE
terms.definition: A entity capable of being placed on a SECURITY LIST. Notes: Identifier of a SECURITY LISTABLE.

terms.label: OM Dated Vehicle Journey Interchange MODEL::DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE
terms.definition: A VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE between two DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs. It could be created ad-hoc or be based on a planned interchange such as a SERVICE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE, a SERVICE JOURNEY PATTERN INTERCHANGE, or an INTERCHANGE RULE. Notes: An indicator if the interchange should be advertised to the public or not. Notes: The latest time that the distributor vehicle can delay its departure to in the wait for a delayed feeder vehicle. Notes: Identifier of DATED VEHICLE INTERCHANGE. Notes: The shortest time needed for a passenger to traverse the distance from the arrival point of the feeder vehicle to the departure point of the distributor vehicle. Notes: A special marker indicating if the feeder and distributor vehicle journey are run by the same vehicle.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Detecting MODEL::DETECTED OPERATION
terms.definition: An actual data detected in a VEHICLE DETECTING event: detection of an actual vehicle coupling, of an INCIDENT, of an actual relief, etc. Notes: Identifier of DETECTED OPERATION. Notes: Type of DETECTED OPERATION, e.g. doors opening.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Detecting MODEL::TYPE OF VEHICLE DETECTING
terms.definition: A characterisation of the detection activity. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF VEHICLE DETECTING.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Detecting MODEL::VEHICLE DETECTING
terms.definition: An activity consisting in the identification of a vehicle at a certain time by a detection device and of collecting crude data such as an absolute location of the vehicle. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE DETECTING. Notes: Time of VEHICLE DETECTING.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Detecting MODEL::VEHICLE DETECTING LOG ENTRY
terms.definition: A record of detected crude real time data that is recognized to be related with a certain VEHICLE. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE DETECTING LOG ENTRY.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::IMPEDED TIME
terms.definition: The difference between the impeded and non-impeded passage of a LINK. It consists of slow down time, waiting time, and accelerating time. Notes: The distance covered during the IMPEDED TIME. Notes: The location,in relation to the start of link, where the IMPEDED TIME began. Notes: Time when the IMPEDED TIME ended. Notes: Identifier of IMPEDED TIME. Notes: Time when the IMPEDED TIME began.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::MONITORED OPERATION
terms.definition: An operational data monitored in a VEHICLE MONITORING event (e.g. monitoring a LOGICAL VEHICLE, coupled to others, as operating a planned TRAIN BLOCK). Notes: Identifier of MONITORED OPERATION. Notes: The type of MONITORED OPERATION, e.g. vehicle coupling, parking, driver relief.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::MONITORED SPECIAL SERVICE
terms.definition: A special service that is monitored as being operated by a LOGICAL VEHICLE. Notes: Identifier of MONITORED SPECIAL SERVICE.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY
terms.definition: A journey that is monitored as being operated by a LOGICAL VEHICLE. According to the monitoring system capabilities, a MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY may be related to a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY, or only to a JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Identifier of MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::TYPE OF VEHICLE MONITORING
terms.definition: The aspect (type of situation) addressed by the monitoring activity. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF VEHICLE MONITORING.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::VEHICLE MONITORING
terms.definition: An activity consisting in the assignment, at a certain time, of operational data to a monitored LOGICAL VEHICLE (e.g. that the vehicle is operating a certain MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY, or has passed at a certain OBSERVED PASSING TIME at a POINT). Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE MONITORING. Notes: Time of VEHICLE MONITORING.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Monitoring MODEL::VEHICLE MONITORING LOG ENTRY
terms.definition: A record of computed information describing some aspect of how a certain LOGICAL VEHICLE performs in relation to the latest operation plan based on comparing information from detection devices with operational data. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE MONITORING LOG ENTRY.

terms.label: OM Monitored Passing Times MODEL::ESTIMATED PASSING TIME
terms.definition: A time data, calculated from the latest available input, about when a public transport vehicle will pass a particular POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN on a specified DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY. These are mainly used to inform passengers about expected times of arrival and/or departure, but may also be used for monitoring and re-planning. Notes: Expected arrival time. Notes: Expected departure time. Notes: Expected time of passing if not stopping. Notes: Expected time to be spent at the stop between arrival and departure. Notes: Identifier of ESTIMATED PASSING TIME.

terms.label: OM Monitored Passing Times MODEL::OBSERVED PASSING TIME
terms.definition: The actual passing of a public transport vehicle at a pre-defined POINT during a MONITORED VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Actual arrival time. Notes: Actual departure time. Notes: Actual passing time (if not stopping). Notes: Actual time spent at the stop between the arrival and the departure. Notes: Identifier of OBSERVED PASSING TIME.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Control Action MODEL::VEHICLE CONTROL ACTION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION affecting the LOGICAL VEHICLE. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE CONTROL ACTION.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Control Action MODEL::CHANGE OF VEHICLE
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in removing, at a certain point in time and space, all work assigned to a LOGICAL VEHICLE and of assigning it to another LOGICAL VEHICLE. Notes: Identifier of CHANGE OF VEHICLE. Notes: Time of CHANGE OF VEHICLE.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Control Action MODEL::LOGICAL VEHICLE CANCELLATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in removing a LOGICAL VEHICLE from the production plan. Notes: Identifier of LOGICAL VEHICLE CANCELLATION.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Control Action MODEL::LOGICAL VEHICLE CREATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in creating a completely new LOGICAL VEHICLE and assigning DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs to the new LOGICAL VEHICLE. Notes: Identifier of LOGICAL VEHICLE CREATION.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Control Action MODEL::VEHICLE ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The assignment, or the cancellation of an assignment, of a physical VEHICLE to a LOGICAL VEHICLE. This assignment may be overridden by a further assignment. Notes: Indication if the action is to assign or cancel a VEHICLE ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: OM Vehicle Control Action MODEL::VEHICLE WORK ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: The assignment, or the cancellation of an assignment, of a LOGICAL VEHICLE to a planned work, represented as DATED BLOCKs or as DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs. This assignment may be overridden by a further assignment. Notes: Indication if the action is to assign or cancel a VEHICLE WORK ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Identifier of VEHICLE WORK ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::ELEMENTARY JOURNEY CONTROL ACTION
terms.definition: A non-composite CONTROL ACTION affecting DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs. Notes: Identifier of ELEMENTARY JOURNEY CONTROL ACTION.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::FLEXIBLE JOURNEY ACTIVATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in activating a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY that has a booking pre-condition. Notes: Identifier of FLEXIBLE JOURNEY ACTIVATION.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::PARTIAL JOURNEY CANCELLATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in assigning a JOURNEY PATTERN that is a subset of the original JOURNEY PATTERN to a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY; thus specifically expressing that a part of a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY has been cancelled. Notes: Identifier of PARTIAL JOURNEY CANCELLATION.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::CHANGE OF JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in assigning a new JOURNEY PATTERN (and the ROUTE supporting it) to a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of CHANGE OF JOURNEY PATTERN.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::CHANGE OF JOURNEY TIMING
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in changing one or several characteristics of a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY, in particular the departure time of the journey. Notes: Identifier of CHANGE OF JOURNEY TIMING. Notes: New intended departure time of journey.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::JOURNEY CANCELLATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in deleting a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY from the latest valid plan. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY CANCELLATION.

terms.label: OM Elementary Journey Control Action MODEL::JOURNEY CREATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in adding a completely new DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY to the latest valid plan. Notes: Identifier of JOURNEY CREATION.

terms.label: OM CA Composite Journey Control Action MODEL

terms.definition: OM Composite Journey Control Action MODEL : Public Package Created: 08/05/2017 07:54:20 Modified: 25/04/2021 12:40:18 Project: Author: Ulf Bjersing Version: 6.0-1.0 Phase: 1.0 Status: Validated Complexity: Easy Difficulty: Priority: Multiplicity: Advanced: UUID: {B66E319C-B7AC-493a-86A6-98706EDEB524} Appears In:

terms.label: OM Composite Journey Control Action MODEL::COMPOSITE JOURNEY CONTROL ACTION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION affecting a set of DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs with a correlated set of adjustments. Notes: Identifier of COMPOSITE JOURNEY CONTROL ACTION.

terms.label: OM Composite Journey Control Action MODEL::DEPARTURE EXCHANGE
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in permuting at one POINT the departure times of two or several DATED VEHICLE JOURNEYs. Notes: Identifier of DEPARTURE EXCHANGE. Notes: Permutation direction of DEPARTURE EXCHANGE, i.e. ascending or descending.

terms.label: OM Composite Journey Control Action MODEL::DEPARTURE LAG
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in gradually shifting a set of departures at one POINT. It allows a change of the timetable without abrupt variations in the intervals. Notes: Identifier of DEPARTURE LAG. Notes: Time value expressing the difference between planned time and intended time when DEPARTURE LAG is fully applied.

terms.label: OM Composite Journey Control Action MODEL::RESORPTION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in progressively resorbing a delay on one DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY by rescheduling the departure times at one POINT of the following journeys. It is a way of maintaining regular intervals after a disturbance on a particular journey. Notes: Identifier of RESORPTION. Notes: Time value expressing the intended reduction of delay for each subsequent journey.

terms.label: OM Composite Journey Control Action MODEL::RESPACING
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in respacing departure times at one POINT after a journey or a vehicle has been added or canceled, in order to preserve the regularity of intervals. Notes: Identifier of RESPACING.

terms.label: OM Interchange Control Action MODEL::INTERCHANGE CANCELLATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in deleting a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE from the latest valid plan so that a distributor DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY no longer needs to wait for a feeder DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE CANCELLATION.

terms.label: OM Interchange Control Action MODEL::INTERCHANGE CONTROL ACTION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION affecting a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE CONTROL ACTION.

terms.label: OM Interchange Control Action MODEL::INTERCHANGE CREATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION consisting in adding a completely new DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE between a feeder DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY and a distributor DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY to the latest valid plan. Notes: An indicator if the interchange should be advertised to the public or not. Notes: The latest time that the distributor vehicle can delay its departure to in the wait for passengers from a delayed feeder vehicle. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE CREATION. Notes: The shortest time needed for a passenger to traverse the distance from the arrival point of the feeder vehicle to the departure point of the distributor vehicle. Notes: An indicator if the feeder and distributor vehicle journey are run by the same vehicle.

terms.label: OM Interchange Control Action MODEL::INTERCHANGE MODIFICATION
terms.definition: A CONTROL ACTION expressing that the duration a distributor DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY needs to wait for a feeder DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY in a DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY INTERCHANGE is changed or that a different DATED VEHICLE JOURNEY is to wait for the feeder. Notes: The latest time that the distributor vehicle can delay its departure to in the wait for passengers from a delayed feeder vehicle. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGE MODIFICATION.

terms.label: OM Operational Event & Incident MODEL::OPERATIONAL EVENT
terms.definition: Any event affecting the public transport operation (production follow-up, management of information or the technical functioning), occurring on an OPERATING DAY and recorded in the system. An OPERATIONAL EVENT is generally causing a CONTROL ACTION. Notes: Description of OPERATIONAL EVENT. Notes: Identifier of OPERATIONAL EVENT. Notes: Time of OPERATIONAL EVENT.

terms.label: OM Operational Event & Incident MODEL::ALARM
terms.definition: An EVENT alerting the staff in charge of operations control on a probable dysfunction: operational threshold exceeded (e.g. delay), emergency call, failure, etc. Notes: Identifier of ALARM.

terms.label: OM Operational Event & Incident MODEL::FACILITY OPERATIONAL EVENT
terms.definition: An OPERATIONAL EVENT concerning a FACILITY. Notes: Identifier of FACILITY OPERATIONAL EVENT.

terms.label: OM Operational Event & Incident MODEL::SITE OPERATIONAL EVENT
terms.definition: An OPERATIONAL EVENT applying to a SITE. Notes: Identifier of SITE OPERATIONAL EVENT.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::RELATED SITUATION
terms.definition: A partial or alternate view of the same SITUATION. Notes: Identifier of RELATED SITUATION. Notes: Categorisation if the viewed SITUATION is a partial or alternate view of the referenced SITUATION.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::SITUATION
terms.definition: An incident or deviation affecting traffic or travel circumstances. Notes: Identifier of SITUATION. Notes: Describes the overall processing state of the SITUATION, e.g. 'Draft' for not yet published; 'Published' for live SITUATIONs; 'Closed' for a completed SITUATION. Notes: Unique identifier of SITUATION within a Participant that is retained across all versions of the SITUATION.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::SITUATION CAUSE
terms.definition: An event or set of events inducing a change in public transport or traffic operation. Notes: Identifier of SITUATION CAUSE.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::SITUATION REASON
terms.definition: A classification of what caused the SITUATION. Notes: Identifier of REASON.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::SITUATION SOURCE
terms.definition: A description of the origin of the incident or deviation information. Notes: Reference to an agent, i.e. the capture client user who input a SITUATION. Notes: Identifier of SITUATION SOURCE. Notes: Name of SITUATION SOURCE. Notes: Electronic file / attachment containing the source information for the SITUATION. Notes: Time when the source information was communicated, if different from creation time.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::METHOD OF CAPTURE
terms.definition: A classification of the method used to acquire knowledge of the deviation or incident. Notes: Identifier of METHOD OF CAPTURE.

terms.label: OM Base Situation MODEL::TYPE OF SITUATION SOURCE
terms.definition: A classification of the SITUATION SOURCE. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF SITUATION SOURCE.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::PT SITUATION
terms.definition: An incident or deviation affecting the planned PT operatioTransmodeln. Notes: Identifier of PT SITUATION.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::PT SITUATION AFFECTED SCOPE
terms.definition: An extent directly involved in the PT SITUATION expressed using entities such as OPERATORs, NETWORKs, LINEs, SCHEDULED STOP POINTs, STOP PLACEs, PLACEs etc. Notes: Affected overall geographic scope. Notes: Identifier of SITUATION AFFECTED SCOPE.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::PT SITUATION CONSEQUENCE SCOPE
terms.definition: An extent impacted by the PT SITUATION CONSEQUENCE expressed using entities such as LINEs, SERVICE JOURNEYs etc. Notes: Affected overall geographic scope. Notes: Identifier of SITUATION CONSEQUENCE SCOPE.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::PT SITUATION CONSEQUENCE
terms.definition: A description of the consequences of the PT SITUATION generally or in relation to involved or indirectly impacted public transport elements. Notes: Advice to passengers in impacted PT SCOPE. Notes: Classification of effect on impacted PT SCOPE, i.e. TPEG Pti13 Service Condition values. Notes: Description of PT SITUATION CONSEQUENCE. Notes: Identifier of SITUATION CONSEQUENCE. Notes: Severity of disruption for impacted PT SCOPE.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::TYPE OF DELAY
terms.definition: A classification of the delay. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF DELAY.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::CASUALTIES
terms.definition: A description of the number of persons that have been injured or died. Notes: Identifier of CASUALTIES. Notes: Number of fatalities. Notes: Number of injured persons.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::DELAY
terms.definition: A description of deviations from the public transport timetable. Notes: Additional journey time needed to overcome disruption. Notes: Characterization of delay. Notes: Identifier of DELAY.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::EASEMENT
terms.definition: A description of temporary (fare) exceptions allowed because of disruptions. Notes: Description of fare exceptions allowed because of the disruption. Notes: Identifier of EASEMENT.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::PT SITUATION GENERAL CONSEQUENCE
terms.definition: A parameter describing a general consequence of a PT SITUATION. Notes: Identifier of PT SITUATION GENERAL CONSEQUENCE.

terms.label: OM PT Situation MODEL::PT SITUATION MESSAGE
terms.definition: An information communicated concerning a certain PT SITUATION. Notes: Identifier of PT SITUATION MESSAGE.

terms.definition: A FACILITY STATUS categorizes the change to availability of the facility, such as being removed, unavailable or only partially available. Notes: Identifier of FACILITY STATUS. Notes: Characterization of the FACILITY STATUS, e.g. removed, unavailable.

terms.label: OM Facility Condition MODEL::PLANNED REMEDY

terms.label: OM Facility Condition MODEL::REMEDY
terms.definition: A general or planned counter-measure to compensate a deviating FACILITY CONDITION. Notes: Identifier of REMEDY. Notes: Characterization of the REMEDY, e.g. utilizing an alternative FACILITY.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL
terms.definition: Describes shared pricing parameters used in the Fare Model

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::PRICE UNIT
terms.definition: A unit to express prices: amount of currency, abstract fare unit, ticket unit or token etc. Notes: Identifier of PRICE UNIT. Notes: Name of PRICE UNIT.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::PRICING PARAMETER SET
terms.definition: A set of parameters controlling pricing calculations. Notes: Whether cumulative discounts are generally allowed. Notes: Identifier of PRICING PARAMETER SET. . Notes: Name of method to use for pricing. Notes: Default ROUNDING parameters to use

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::ROUNDING
terms.definition: Parameters directing the rounding of values that are the result of calculations. Notes: Identifier of ROUNDING. Notes: Name of ROUNDING.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::ROUNDING METHOD
terms.definition: A classification of PRICING RULES. Notes: Identifier of ROUNDING METHOD.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::ROUNDING STEP
terms.definition: Parameters to determine the rounding value to be used for a given calculation result. If a rounding step table is used, any value equal to or larger than the step key and smaller that the next step key should be rounded to the value indicated for the step value. Notes: Identifier of ROUNDING STEP. Notes: Start value for range; round if result value greater than range key and less than range key of next step table value. Notes: Value to which to round.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF PRICING RULE
terms.definition: A classification of a PRICING RULE. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PRICING RULE.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::PRICING RULE
terms.definition: A rule used for the calculation of FARE PRICE, determined either by a set of parameters to be applied to a reference price or by a more complex algorithm. PRICING RULEs may be chained together. Notes: Description of PRICING RULE. Notes: Identifier of PRICING RULE Notes: Whether the PRICING RULE is used to calculate tax. Notes: Method Name of PRICING RULE. Notes: URL for info associated with PRICING RULE.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::LIMITING RULE
terms.definition: A rule for limiting the results of a price calculation. Notes: Identifier of LIMITING RULE Notes: Maximum limit expressed as a percentage of the total price. Notes: Limiting amount above which resulting fare may not be sold. Notes: Maximum price above which resulting fare may not be sold. Notes: Maximum PRICE expressed as a multiple of a unit fare. Notes: Maximum PRICE expressed as a percentage of the total price. Notes: Minimum limit expressed as a percentage of the total price. Notes: Limiting amount below which resulting fare may not be sold. Notes: Minimum price below which resulting fare may not be sold. Notes: Minimum PRICE expressed as a multiple of a unit fare. Notes: Minimum PRICE expressed as a percentage of the total price.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::DISCOUNTING RULE
terms.definition: A price calculation rule determined by a discount. Notes: Whether discount can be used cumulatively in combination with other discounts. Notes: Discount of PRICE as a percentage. Notes: Discount of PRICE as a value. Notes: Identifier of DISCOUNTING RULE.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::PRICING SERVICE
terms.definition: A web service used to provide prices dynamically at time of booking or purchase. Notes: Description of PRICING SERVICE. Notes: Identifier of PRICING SERVICE. Notes: Name of PRICING SERVICE. Notes: Url at which service is available.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::FARE DAY TYPE
terms.definition: A type of day used in the fare collection domain, characterised by one or more properties which affect the definition of access rights and prices in the fare system. Notes: Identifier of FARE DAY TYPE.

terms.label: FP Fare Calculation Parameters MODEL::MONTH VALIDITY OFFSET
terms.definition: Days before (negative) or after (positive) the start of the month that a product with a calendar period driven activation becomes valid. Notes: Number days relative to start of month. Notes: Identifier of MONTH VALIDITY OFFSET Notes: Name of Month Validity Offset

terms.label: FP Fare Price MODEL
terms.definition: Describes common Price components used in the Fare Model

terms.label: FP Fare Price MODEL::PRICEABLE OBJECT
terms.definition: An element which may have a FARE PRICE. Notes: Description of PRICEABLE OBJECT. Notes: Identifier of PRICEABLE OBJECT. Notes: Name of PRICEABLE OBJECT.

terms.label: FP Fare Price MODEL::FARE PRICE
terms.definition: Price features for a PRICEABLE OBJECT. Notes: Price in a specified currency. Notes: Discount given, if any, in a specified currency. Notes: Discount percentage used, if any when deriving price. Notes: End date for PRICE validity. Notes: Identifier of FARE PRICE. Notes: Whether the FARE PRICE is allowed. Default is true. Notes: Name of PRICE. Notes: Relative ranking to be given to discount to use to favour it over other discounts available. Notes: Start date for PRICE validity. Notes: Tax included in Amount, in same currency as amount. Notes: Tax rate used, if any when deriving price.

terms.label: FP Fare Price MODEL::PRICE GROUP
terms.definition: A grouping of prices, allowing the grouping of numerous possible consumption elements into a limited number of price references, or to apply grouped increase, in value or percentage. Notes: End date for PRICE validity for prices in the group. This overrides any date on an individual price in the group. Notes: Identifier of PRICE GROUP. Notes: Start date for PRICE validity for prices in the group. This overrides any date on an individual price in the group.

terms.label: FP Parking Tariff MODEL
terms.definition: Describes Price components used in the Parking Model

terms.label: FP Parking Tariff MODEL::PARKING TARIFF
terms.definition: A set of parking CHARGE BANDS that describe the cost of using a PARKING or PARKING AREA. Notes: Whether additional tax is charged on top of rates. Notes: Identifier of PARKING TARIFF. Notes: Reference to PARKING STAY TYPE of PARKING TARIFF.

terms.label: FP Parking Tariff MODEL::PARKING CHARGE BAND
terms.definition: Parking charges that describe the cost of using a PARKING or PARKING AREA for a given period. Notes: Identifier of PARKING CHARGE BAND. Notes: Maximum stay for PARKING CHARGE BAND.

terms.label: FP Parking Tariff MODEL::PARKING PRICE
terms.definition: A specialisation of FARE PRICE that defines the price of a PARKING CHARGE BAND. Notes: Identifier of PARKING TARIFF PRICE.

terms.label: FP Parking Tariff MODEL::TYPE OF STAY
terms.definition: A classification of the type of parking stay, e.g. long term, short term; may be used to choose pricing criteria. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF STAY.

terms.label: FP Fare Table MODEL
terms.definition: Describes the FARE TABLE components used to organise FARE PRICEs

terms.label: FP Fare Table MODEL::FARE TABLE
terms.definition: A grouping of prices (specialization of PRICE GROUP) that may be associated with all or any of DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT, FARE STRUCTURE ELEMENT GEOGRAPHICAL INTERVAL, GROUP OF ACCESS RIGHT PARAMETER, CLASS OF USE, OPERATOR, VEHICLE MODE, FARE PRODUCT. Notes: Data is to be kept private until the stated date. Notes: End date for PRICE validity for prices in the group. This overrides any date on an individual price in the group. Notes: Identifier of FARE TABLE. Notes: Start date for PRICE validity for prices in the group. This overrides any date on an individual price in the group.

terms.label: FP Fare Table MODEL::CELL
terms.definition: An unique individual combination of features within a FARE TABLE, used to associate a FARE PRICE with a fare element. Notes: Identifier of CELL. Notes: Name of CELL. Notes: Order in which cell appears within table.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL
terms.definition: Describes the network related aspects of the FARE STRUCTURE.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::FARE ZONE
terms.definition: A specialization of TARIFF ZONE to include FARE SECTIONs. Notes: Identifier of FARE ZONE.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::BORDER POINT
terms.definition: A POINT on the network marking a boundary for the fare calculation. May or may not be a SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: Description of BORDER POINT. Notes: Identifier of BORDER POINT. Notes: Short Name of BORDER POINT.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::FARE POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN
terms.definition: A POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN which represents the start or end of a FARE SECTION, or a point used to define a SERIES CONSTRAINT. Notes: Relative ranking for showing this FARE POINT when abridging a series pattern. e.g. 1.= can be deleted first, 2=can be deleted second, etc. Notes: Identifier of a FARE POINT IN JOURNEY PATTERN. Notes: Whether interchange to another service is allowed at this point Notes: Relative position for showing this

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::FARE SCHEDULED STOP POINT
terms.definition: A specialisation of SCHEDULED STOP POINT describing a stop with fare accounting and routing characteristics. Notes: Identifier of FARE SCHEDULED STOP POINT. Notes: Name to use to indicate Station on Routings.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::FARE SECTION
terms.definition: A subdivision of a JOURNEY PATTERN consisting of consecutive POINTs IN JOURNEY PATTERN, used to define an element of the fare structure. Notes: Identifier of FARE SECTION. Notes: Name of FARE SECTION.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::SERIES CONSTRAINT
terms.definition: An extension of a DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT (a cell of an origin-destination matrix for TARIFF ZONEs or SCHEDULED STOP POINTs) expressing a fare distance for the corresponding trip (value in km, number of fare units etc.), constrained to specific routes. SERIES CONSTRAINTs are mainly used for rail fares. Notes: Whether series can only be used by itself, or whether it can be used in a chain of series Notes: Notional distance along SERIES CONSTRAINT for computation of First Class fares. Notes: Identifier of SERIES CONSTRAINT. Notes: Text description of Series See Tap TSI 5.1 Notes: Relative priority of this pattern when there are multiple SERIES CONSTRAINTs between the same points. (Equivalent to route number on TAP TSI Series Number). Notes: Notional distance along SERIES CONSTRAINT for computation of Second Class fares.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::SERIES CONSTRAINT PRICE
terms.definition: A set of all possible price features of a SERIES CONSTRAINT: default total price etc. Notes: Identifer of SERIES CONSTRAINT PRICE.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::TYPE OF SERIES CONSTRAINT
terms.definition: A classification of a SERIES CONSTRAINT. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF SERIES CONSTRAINT.

terms.label: FZ Fare Zone MODEL::TYPE OF ROUTING
terms.definition: A classification of the ROUTING, e.g. direct, indirect; may be used to choose pricing criteria. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ROUTING.

terms.definition: An interval based aspect of the fare structure. Notes: Identifier of FARE INTERVAL.

terms.label: FS Common Fare Structure MODEL::FARE STRUCTURE FACTOR
terms.definition: A factor influencing access rights definition or calculation of prices. Notes: Value associated with factor. Notes: Identifier of FARE STRUCTURE FACTOR.

terms.label: FS Common Fare Structure MODEL::FARE UNIT
terms.definition: A unit associated with a FARE STRUCTURE FACTOR. Notes: Identifier of FARE UNIT.

terms.label: FS Common Fare Structure MODEL::FARE ELEMENT IN SEQUENCE
terms.definition: A part of an access right, including its possible order in the sequence of elementary access rights. Notes: Identifier of FARE ELEMENT IN SEQUENCE. terms.definition: Describes spatial elements used in the FARE STRUCTURE.

terms.label: FS Geographical Fare Structure MODEL::GEOGRAPHICAL STRUCTURE FACTOR
terms.definition: The value of a GEOGRAPHICAL INTERVAL or a DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT expressed by a GEOGRAPHICAL UNIT. Notes: Identifier of GEOGRAPHICAL STRUCTURE FACTOR.

terms.label: FS Geographical Fare Structure MODEL::GEOGRAPHICAL UNIT

terms.label: FS Geographical Fare Structure MODEL::GEOGRAPHICAL UNIT PRICE
terms.definition: A set of all possible price features of a GEOGRAPHICAL UNIT: default total price etc.

terms.definition: Describes elements used to define point to point and zone to zone fares structures.

terms.label: FS Distance Matrix Element MODEL::DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT
terms.definition: A cell of an origin-destination matrix for TARIFF ZONEs or SCHEDULED STOP POINTs, expressing a fare distance for the corresponding trip: value in km, number of fare units etc. Notes: Distance between origin and destination of a DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT. Notes: Identifier of a DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT. Notes: Relative preference assigned to this element if there are multiple entries between two points.

terms.label: FS Distance Matrix Element MODEL::DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENT PRICE

terms.label: FS Distance Matrix Element MODEL::GROUP OF DISTANCE MATRIX ELEMENTS

terms.definition: Describes temporal elements used in the FARE STRUCTURE.

terms.label: FS Time Fare Structure MODEL::TIME INTERVAL

terms.label: FS Time Fare Structure MODEL::TIME STRUCTURE FACTOR
terms.definition: The value of a TIME INTERVAL expressed by a TIME UNIT. Notes: Identifier of TIME STRUCTURE FACTOR.

terms.label: FS Time Fare Structure MODEL::TIME UNIT
terms.definition: A unit for calculating time-based graduated fares. Notes: Duration of TIME UNIT (e.g. 2, if the duration is 2 hours). Notes: Identifier of TIME UNIT.

terms.label: FS Time Fare Structure MODEL::TIME UNIT PRICE
terms.definition: A set of all possible price features of a TIME UNIT: default total price etc. Notes: Identifier of TIME UNIT PRICE.

terms.definition: Describes quality and quota based elements used in the FARE STRUCTURE.

terms.label: FS Quality Fare Structure MODEL::QUALITY STRUCTURE FACTOR

terms.label: FS Quality Fare Structure MODEL::QUALITY STRUCTURE FACTOR PRICE
terms.definition: A set of all possible price features of a QUALITY STRUCTURE FACTOR , e.g. default total price etc. Notes: Identifier of QUALITY STRUCTURE FACTOR PRICE.

terms.label: FS Quality Fare Structure MODEL::FARE DEMAND FACTOR
terms.definition: A named set of parameters defining a period of travel with a given price, for example off peak, peak, super off peak, etc. Notes: Identifier of a FARE DEMAND FACTOR.

terms.label: FS Quality Fare Structure MODEL::START TIME AT STOP POINT
terms.definition: A time at which a fare time band (peak, off peak, etc ) is deemed to begin for trips starting at a particular station. Notes: Day offset of end time from start time. If same day, zero. Notes: Time at which timeband ends at station. Notes: Identifier of START TIME AT STOP POINT. Notes: Time at which timeband starts at station.

terms.label: FS Quality Fare Structure MODEL::FARE QUOTA FACTOR

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL
terms.definition: Describes different types of Fare product.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::ENTITLEMENT PRODUCT
terms.definition: A precondition to access a service or to purchase a FARE PRODUCT issued by an organisation that may not be a PT operator (e.g. military card). Notes: Identifier of ENTITLEMENT PRODUCT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::THIRD PARTY PRODUCT
terms.definition: A FARE PRODUCT that is marketed together with a Public Transport FARE PRODUCT. Notes: Identifier of THIRD PARTY PRODUCT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::ACCESS RIGHT IN PRODUCT
terms.definition: A VALIDABLE ELEMENT as a part of a PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT, including its possible order in the set of all VALIDABLE ELEMENTs grouped together to define the access right assigned to that PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT. Notes: Identifier of ACCESS RIGHT IN PRODUCT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::SALE DISCOUNT RIGHT
terms.definition: A FARE PRODUCT allowing a customer to benefit from discounts when purchasing SALES OFFER PACKAGEs. Notes: Identifier of SALE DISCOUNT RIGHT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::AMOUNT OF PRICE UNIT
terms.definition: A FARE PRODUCT consisting in a stored value of PRICE UNITs: an amount of money on an electronic purse, amount of units on a value card etc. Notes: Amount in a specified PRICE UNIT. Notes: Identifier of AMOUNT OF PRICE UNIT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::CAPPED DISCOUNT RIGHT
terms.definition: A specialisation of SALE DISCOUNT RIGHT where the discount is expressed as a rule specifying a ceiling for a given time interval. For example, the London Oyster card fare, which charges for each journey until travel equivalent to a day pass has been consumed after which further travel is free at that day. Notes: Identifier of CAPPED DISCOUNT RIGHT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::CAPPING RULE
terms.definition: A capping limit for a given time interval, where the capping is expressed by another product. For example, the London Oyster card fare, which charges for each journey until travel equivalent to a day pass for the mode of travel has been consumed. Notes: Identifier of CAPPING RULE. Notes: Capping distance if distance based cap.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::CAPPING RULE PRICE
terms.definition: A set of all possible price features of a CAPPING RULE: default total price, discount in value or percentage etc. Notes: Identifier of CAPPING RULE PRICE.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT
terms.definition: A FARE PRODUCT consisting of one or several VALIDABLE ELEMENTs, specific to a CHARGING MOMENT . Notes: Identifier of PREASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::SUPPLEMENT PRODUCT
terms.definition: A PRE-ASSIGNED FARE PRODUCT that will provide additional right when used with (as a complement of) another (reserved seat, second to first class upgrade, etc.). SUPPLEMENT PRODUCT also usually means supplement price. Notes: Identifier of SUPPLEMENT PRODUCT.

terms.label: AR Types of Fare Product MODEL ::USAGE DISCOUNT RIGHT
terms.definition: A FARE PRODUCT allowing a customer to benefit from discounts when consuming VALIDABLE ELEMENTs. Notes: Identifier of USAGE DISCOUNT RIGHT.

Notes: Name of ACCESS RIGHT PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT. Notes: Nature of comparison with assignment values Notes: Operator to use to combine Validity Parameter elements.

terms.label: AR Access Right Parameter Assignment MODEL::GENERIC PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT

terms.label: AR Access Right Parameter Assignment MODEL::SPECIFIC PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT

terms.label: AR Access Right Parameter Assignment MODEL::VALIDITY PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: An ACCESS RIGHT PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT relating a fare collection parameter to a theoretical FARE PRODUCT (or one of its components) or a SALES OFFER PACKAGE. Notes: Identifier of VALIDITY PARAMETER ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: AR Access Right Parameter Assignment MODEL::TYPE OF ACCESS RIGHT ASSIGNMENT
terms.definition: A classification of ACCESS RIGHT ASSIGNMENT to indicate the purpose of the assignment. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF ACCESS RIGHT ASSIGNMENT.

terms.label: AR Charging Usage Parameters MODEL::CHARGING POLICY
terms.definition: A parameter governing minimum amount and credit allowed when consuming a FARE PRODUCT. Notes: Period by which adjustment or rebate must be collected or will be retracted. Notes: Identifier of CHARGING POLICY.

terms.label: AR Charging Usage Parameters MODEL::PENALTY POLICY
terms.definition: Parameters determining a policy regarding different aspects of penalty charges, for example repeated entry at the same station, not having a ticket etc. Notes: Identifier of PENALTY POLICY. Notes: Minimum period before reentry at same station allowed without incurring penalty action.

terms.label: AR Charging Usage Parameters MODEL::SUBSCRIBING
terms.definition: Parameters governing subscription to a product allowing payment at regular intervals. Notes: Identifier of SUBSCRIBING. Notes: Allowed means of payment of installations as standard value. Notes: Maximum duration allowed for a subscription. Notes: Minimum duration allowed for a subscription. Notes: Policy on renewing subscription..

terms.label: AR Charging Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF CREDIT POLICY
terms.definition: A classification of CREDIT POLICY, to apply if user runs out of funds on account or stored value card. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF CREDIT POLICY.

terms.label: AR Charging Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF PENALTY POLICY
terms.definition: A classification of PENALTY POLICY, for example no fare, excess fare, etc. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PENALTY POLICY.

terms.label: AR Charging Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF RE-ENTRY POLICY
terms.definition: A classification of RE ENTRY POLICY, if user renters a station within a specified time limit. no fare, max fare, etc. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF REENTRY POLICY.

terms.label: AR Validity Parameters MODEL::SERVICE VALIDITY PARAMETER

terms.label: AR Validity Parameters MODEL::ORGANISATIONAL VALIDITY PARAMETER
terms.definition: A type of VALIDITY PARAMETER related to organisational issues . Notes: Identifier of ORGANISATIONAL VALIDITY PARAMETER.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL
terms.definition: Describes diverse conditions on how access rights may be consumed when travelling..

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::STEP LIMIT
terms.definition: Geographical parameter limiting the access rights by counts of stops, sections or zones. Notes: Identifier of STEP LIMIT parameter. Notes: Maximum number of steps that can be made. Notes: Minimum number of Trips that can be made. Notes: Minimum number of steps that must be made. Notes: Whether there is a step limit requirement.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::MINIMUM STAY
terms.definition: Parameters expressing details of any minimum stay at the destination required to use an access right. Notes: Identifier of MINIMUM STAY parameter. Notes: Minimum number of nights that can be spent away. Notes: Minimum number of nights that must be spent away.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::ROUND TRIP
terms.definition: Parameters relating to single or return trip use of an access right. Notes: Identifier of ROUND TRIP. Notes: Whether return trip is required. Notes: Whether return trip is allowed. Notes: Whether fare for return trip is single fare doubled

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::ROUTING
terms.definition: Parameters expressing limitations on routing of an access right. Notes: Whether the routing is across a border. Notes: Identifier of ROUTING. Notes: Whether only allowed on certain routes or series Notes: Return route must be same as outbound route

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::FREQUENCY OF USE
terms.definition: The limits of usage frequency for a FARE PRODUCT (or one of its components) or a SALES OFFER PACKAGE during a specific VALIDITY PERIOD. There may be different prices depending on how often the right is consumed during the period. Notes: Identifier of FREQUENCY OF USE. Notes: Maximum number of times can be used. Notes: Minimum number of times can be used.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD
terms.definition: A time limitation for validity of a FARE PRODUCT or a SALES OFFER PACKAGE. It may be composed of a standard duration (e.g. 3 days, 1 month) and/or fixed start/end dates and times. Notes: End date for VALIDITY PERIOD. Notes: End time for VALIDITY PERIOD. Notes: Identifier of USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD. Notes: Duration of VALIDITY PERIOD after departure. or validation Notes: Start Date for VALIDITY PERIOD. Notes: Start time for VALIDITY PERIOD.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::INTERCHANGING
terms.definition: Parameters expressing limitations on making changes within a trip. Notes: Whether the journey can be broken at an interchange point. Notes: Whether the interchange is across a border. Notes: Identifier of INTERCHANGING. Notes: Maximum number of transfers that can be made on a trip. Notes: Maximum time allowed to make a transfer.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF FREQUENCY OF USE
terms.definition: A classification of FREQUENCY OF USE . Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF FREQUENCY OF USE.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF MINIMUM STAY
terms.definition: A classification of MINIMUM STAY requirements. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF MINIMUM STAY.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF USAGE TRIGGER
terms.definition: A classification of the events that may start or end a USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD, for example, 'purchase' 'start of ride', 'end of ride', 'end of day', 'end of period', etc. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF USAGE TRIGGER.

terms.label: AR Travel Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD
terms.definition: A classification of TYPE OF USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF USAGE VALIDITY PERIOD

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL
terms.definition: Describes conditions on who may buy and use a fare product.

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::USER PROFILE
terms.definition: The social profile of a passenger, based on age group, education, profession, social status, sex etc., often used for allowing discounts: 18-40 years old, graduates, drivers, unemployed, women, etc. Notes: Age group required by USER PROFILE. Arbitrary category. Notes: Gender required by USER PROFILE. Relevant for single sex accommodation products. Notes: Identifier of USER PROFILE. Notes: Whether User must be local resident. This is a general categorization. A more specific definition can be provided by RESIDENTIAL QUALIFICATION. Notes: Maximum age for membership of USER PROFILE. Notes: Maximum height for membership of USER PROFILE. This may be relevant for judging large dogs Notes: Minimum age for membership of USER PROFILE. Notes: Minimum height for membership of USER PROFILE. Notes: Day / Month on which age applies. if any.

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::RESIDENTIAL QUALIFICATION
terms.definition: A parameter providing an authorisation to consider a user as being characterised by a USER PROFILE. Notes: Identifier of RESIDENTIAL QUALIFICATIONE. Notes: Whether user must or must not reside in TOPOGRAPHICAL PLACE..

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::COMPANION PROFILE
terms.definition: The number and characteristics of the persons entitled to travel in a group or as companions to another USER PROFILE. Notes: Identifier of COMPANION PROFILE. Notes: Maximum number of persons of this type allowed as companions or GROUP TICKET. Notes: Minimum number of persons of this type allowed as companions or GROUP TICKET.

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::COMMERCIAL PROFILE
terms.definition: A category of users depending on their commercial relations with the operator (frequency of use, amount of purchase etc.), often used for allowing discounts. Notes: Arbitrary factor to be applied when pricing using this factor - in units of consumption. Notes: Arbitrary factor to be applied when pricing using this factor - in price units. Notes: Identifier of COMMERCIAL PROFILE.

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::GROUP TICKET
terms.definition: The number and characteristics of persons entitled to travel in addition to the holder of an access right. Notes: Whether Group Booking required.. Notes: Further special conditions apply. Notes: Identifier of GROUP TICKET. Notes: Whether joint check in is required. Notes: Maximum number of persons overall allowed on GROUP TICKET. Notes: Number of persons for which a group is discount allowed. Notes: Number of persons allowed free on ticket. Notes: Minimum number of persons holding an ENTITLEMENT card or SALES DISCARD needed Notes: Minimum number of persons overall allowed on GROUP TICKET.

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF CONCESSION
terms.definition: A classification of USER PROFILE by type of person eligible to use it. Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF CONCESSION.

terms.label: AR Eligibility Usage Parameters MODEL::TYPE OF PROOF REQUIRED
terms.definition: A classification of TYPEs of PROOF needed to prove eligibility for a USER PROFILE . Notes: Identifier of TYPE OF PROOF REQUIRED.
